title_en: Why Virgin Atlantic Is Targeting The 40 RAF Pilots Keeping Britain's F-35 Fleet Flyable
title_zh: 为什么维珍航空瞄准 40 名英国皇家空军飞行员以保持英国 F-35 机队的飞行能力
summary: Virgin Atlantic has campaigned to entice former RAF fast jet pilots to fly for them on long-haul transatlantic routes.
summary_zh: 维珍航空一直在努力吸引前英国皇家空军快速喷气式飞机飞行员为他们执飞跨大西洋长途航线。
body_en: Aaron is an aviation enthusiast and world traveler with a deep interest in aerospace history and technology. He has traveled around the world numerous times, often incorporating visits to aviation museums and historic aircraft collections into his journeys. A native of New Zealand, he is an expert in aviation and maintains a broad interest in a variety of other subjects.

The United Kingdom only has around four dozen trained F-35B fighter jet pilots and around 150 Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jet pilots. Losing even a handful of these hard-to-replace pilots to commercial airlines is painful. They are targeted by British airlines, with Virgin Atlantic directly targeting them in its recruitment ads in 2024.

As the Royal Air Force is so much smaller than the United States Air Force (and Marines/Navy), it lacks depth in pilots. Training an F-35 fighter jet pilot can cost around $10 million, and new pilots graduating annually in the UK are often measured in the single digits.

With that being said, airlines will typically focus more on military transport pilots, such as those flying A330 MRTTs and A400Ms. Let's examine how Virgin Atlantic seeks to attract ex-RAF pilots and why this is a major problem for the Royal Air Force (and Royal Navy).

In 2024, the publication London Loves Business wrote that " RAF pilots who have operated on F-35 B Lightning II and Typhoon FGR4 are being offered double their annual salary to join Virgin ." It adds that those pilots would be given routes to Barbados and New York to quit the RAF and fly with Virgin Atlantic.

The report stated that the pilots were being offered around double the money that they would typically earn flying for the Royal Air Force. At the time, the Virgin Atlantic advert was reported to read as follows

" In order to be suitable, you must be operating, or have operated in the last three years on one of the following RAF Aircraft: F-35 B Lightning II, Typhoon FGR4. As a member of our Flight Crew, you will be joining the UK’s only exclusively long-haul airline. Flying out of London Heathrow to exciting destinations such as New York, San Francisco, Las Vegas, Delhi, Barbados, Antigua, and many more ."

The advert went on to say that Virgin Atlantic operates the " youngest, cleanest, and most technologically sophisticated " widebody aircraft. Virgin is unusual in exclusively operating a fleet of widebody aircraft. Airlines poaching trained fighter jet pilots is common in many countries , including the United States. For air forces, this can be devastating as it costs around ten million dollars to train a frontline fighter jet pilot and takes years to replace them.

In a typical Western air force, there should be around 1.3 to 1.5 trained pilots for every fast jet. That said, Britain (and other air forces) have struggled to maintain this figure. While the US military has around 37,000 military pilots , including in the USAF, Army (helicopters), Marines, Navy, and Coast Guard, the British military likely has around 2,500.

Of these, around 1,500 are in the RAF and 500 are each in the Royal Navy and British Army. In 2014, the British Government revealed that there were 1,760 trained regular pilots in the RAF (excluding reserves and other aircrew), although that number has likely declined somewhat over the last decade. However, fighter jet pilots are a small subset of the overall group of pilots.

In late 2022, former Defense Secretary Ben Wallace revealed there were only 30 qualified British F-35 pilots, plus three exchange pilots. By 2023, that number had risen to 34, with seven more soon to graduate. By mid-2026, the RAF had received all of its initially ordered 48 F-38Bs, minus one that fell off an aircraft carrier.

Ideally, the RAF should have around 60–70 or so trained F-35B pilots, but it is unclear how many there are. There have been reports that the ratio may be closer to one pilot per jet, suggesting the RAF may now have somewhere around 45 to 50 trained F-35B pilots. Headlines will often talk about the fighter jets, how many there are, and how ready they are, but pilot availability is often a more pressing bottleneck.

The RAF procured a total of 137 Eurofighter Typhoons. Of these, 26 of the Tranche 1 fighter jets have now been retired, leaving a fleet of four remaining. These are stationed at RAF Mount Pleasant in the Falkland Islands as the UK's farthest air base with a permanent fighter jet presence. They are tasked with defending the islands from Argentina and are supported by A400Ms and A330 MRTTs.

The remaining Typhoons include 67 Tranche 2 and 40 Tranche 3 fighter jets. In January 2026, the British Government stated it would upgrade 40 of them with new radars and other systems. In July 2026, the budget was significantly increased, and it was reported that all would be upgraded. Britain had previously said the remaining four Tranche 1 fighter jets would retire in 2027, but now it is unclear.
Select aircraft of the Royal Air Force (per RAF )

There has not been an equivalent public disclosure for how many Typhoon fighter jet pilots are serving in the RAF. A reasonable range would be 140-160 trained Typhoon pilots. This would give the RAF a group of up to 200 fast jet pilots in total. Additionally, as of June 2026, the Royal Air Force had 119 trainee fast-jet pilots progressing through the training pipeline, from RAF Cranwell to the point of starting an Operational Conversion Unit.
Helicopter Pilots Are Less Important In The UK

Beginning around 2015 and then accelerating after COVID-19, the US airline industry has faced an unprecedented pilot shortage. This has affected regional airlines in particular and is made worse by retiring baby boomers. In response, the industry moved to attract former US military helicopter pilots ; previously, the focus had been on fixed-wing pilots.

One of the most famous examples was that of Frontier Airlines, which launched its Rotor Transition Program to help military helicopter pilots transition and receive their fixed-wing qualifications. The program ended up being so successful that, Frontier's website said

" Due to the overwhelmingly positive response and large number of applications we received for our Rotor Transition Program, we have temporarily closed the application window. Keep an eye out for more information regarding the application window opening and future recruitment events. "
body_zh: 亚伦是一位航空爱好者和环球旅行家，对航空航天历史和技术有着浓厚的兴趣。他曾多次环游世界，经常在旅途中参观航空博物馆和历史飞机收藏。他是新西兰人，是航空专家，并对其他各种学科保持着广泛的兴趣。
英国只有约四打训练有素的 F-35B 战斗机飞行员和约 150 名欧洲战斗机台风战斗机飞行员。即使失去少数这些难以替代的飞行员到商业航空公司也是痛苦的。他们是英国航空公司的目标，维珍航空在 2024 年的招聘广告中直接针对他们。
由于英国皇家空军比美国空军（和海军陆战队/海军）小得多，因此缺乏飞行员深度。培训一名 F-35 战斗机飞行员的费用约为 1000 万美元，而英国每年毕业的新飞行员往往只有个位数。
话虽如此，航空公司通常会更多地关注军事运输飞行员，例如驾驶 A330 MRTT 和 A400M 的飞行员。让我们来看看维珍航空如何吸引前英国皇家空军飞行员，以及为什么这对皇家空军（和皇家海军）来说是一个主要问题。
2024 年，《伦敦热爱商业》杂志写道，“曾驾驶过 F-35 B 闪电 II 和台风 FGR4 的英国皇家空军飞行员将获得双倍年薪加入维珍航空。”它还补充说，这些飞行员​​将获得前往巴巴多斯和纽约的航线，以退出英国皇家空军并搭乘维珍航空的航班。
报告称，这些飞行员​​的薪酬大约是他们在皇家空军飞行时通常赚取的两倍左右。据报道，当时维珍航空的广告如下：
“为了符合资格，您必须正在或在过去三年内曾操作过以下英国皇家空军飞机之一：F-35 B Lightning II、台风 FGR4。作为我们飞行机组的一员，您将加入英国唯一的专门长途航空公司。从伦敦希思罗机场飞往纽约、旧金山、拉斯维加斯、德里、巴巴多斯、安提瓜岛等令人兴奋的目的地。”
广告接着说，维珍航空运营着“最年轻、最干净、技术最先进的”宽体飞机。维珍航空在专门运营宽体飞机机队方面与众不同。航空公司挖走训练有素的战斗机飞行员的现象在包括美国在内的许多国家都很常见。对于空军来说，这可能是毁灭性的，因为训练一名前线战斗机飞行员需要花费约一千万美元，并且需要数年时间才能替换他们。
在典型的西方空军中，每架快速喷气式飞机应配备大约 1.3 至 1.5 名训练有素的飞行员。尽管如此，英国（和其他空军）一直在努力维持这一数字。美国军队拥有约 37,000 名军事飞行员，包括美国空军、陆军（直升机）、海军陆战队、海军和海岸警卫队，而英国军队可能拥有约 2,500 名飞行员。
其中，英国皇家空军约有 1,500 人，皇家海军和英国陆军各有 500 人。 2014 年，英国政府透露，英国皇家空军有 1,760 名训练有素的正规飞行员（不包括预备役和其他机组人员），尽管这一数字在过去十年中可能有所下降。然而，战斗机飞行员只是整个飞行员群体的一小部分。
2022 年底，前国防部长本·华莱士透露，英国只有 30 名合格的 F-35 飞行员，外加三名交换飞行员。到 2023 年，这个数字已增至 34 人，还有 7 人即将毕业。到 2026 年中期，英国皇家空军已收到最初订购的 48 架 F-38B 的全部，减去从航空母舰上掉落的一架。
理想情况下，英国皇家空军应该拥有大约 60-70 名训练有素的 F-35B 飞行员，但目前尚不清楚有多少人。有报道称，这一比例可能更接近每架飞机一名飞行员，这表明英国皇家空军现在可能拥有大约 45 至 50 名训练有素的 F-35B 飞行员。头条新闻经常会谈论战斗机、有多少架战斗机以及它们的准备情况如何，但飞行员的可用性往往是一个更紧迫的瓶颈。
英国皇家空军总共采购了 137 架欧洲台风战斗机。其中，26 架第一批战斗机现已退役，只剩下四架战斗机。这些基地驻扎在福克兰群岛的英国皇家空军芒特普莱森特空军基地，这是英国最远的空军基地，拥有永久的战斗机存在。他们的任务是保卫这些岛屿免受阿根廷侵害，并得到 A400M 和 A330 MRTT 的支持。
其余的台风战斗机包括 67 架 2 级战斗机和 40 架 3 级战斗机。 2026 年 1 月，英国政府表示将用新雷达和其他系统升级其中 40 架。 2026年7月，预算大幅增加，据悉将全部升级。英国此前曾表示剩余的四架第一批战斗机将于2027年退役，但现在还不清楚。
英国皇家空军的精选飞机（根据英国皇家空军）
目前还没有公开披露有多少名台风战斗机飞行员在英国皇家空军服役。合理的范围是 140-160 名训练有素的台风飞行员。这将使英国皇家空军拥有总共多达 200 名快速喷气式飞机飞行员。此外，截至 2026 年 6 月，英国皇家空军有 119 名受训快速喷气式飞机飞行员正在通过培训渠道，从英国皇家空军克兰威尔空军基地一直到组建作战转换部队。
直升机飞行员在英国不太重要
从 2015 年左右开始，在新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 疫情之后，美国航空业面临着前所未有的飞行员短缺问题。这尤其影响了支线航空公司，而婴儿潮一代的退休则使情况变得更糟。作为回应，该行业开始吸引前美国军用直升机飞行员；此前，重点是固定翼飞行员。
最著名的例子之一是边疆航空公司，该公司启动了旋翼过渡计划，帮助军用直升机飞行员过渡并获得固定翼资格。 Frontier 网站称，该计划最终非常成功
“ 由于我们的转子转换计划得到了压倒性的积极响应和大量申请，我们暂时关闭了申请窗口。请密切关注有关申请窗口开放和未来招聘活动的更多信息。”

title_en: Why Are All Pratt & Whitney's GTF Engines Green On The Inside?
title_zh: 为什么普惠公司的所有 GTF 发动机内部都是绿色的？
summary: Two engineered components and one practical inspection benefit explain the teal ring inside Pratt & Whitney’s Geared Turbofan.
summary_zh: 两个工程部件和一项实用检查优势解释了普惠公司齿轮传动涡轮风扇发动机内的青色环。
body_en: Jack comes to Simple Flying with a lifelong interest in all things aviation. He holds a degree in Aerospace Engineering from Georgia Tech, and is a certified private and remote pilot. Beyond these experiences, Jack previously worked for a corporate flight department where he gained first-hand experience in the world of business aviation. Currently, Jack works in the professional services industry and continues to build his flight hours outside of work.

Passengers boarding an Airbus A320neo or an A220 who glance at the engine intake from the jet bridge often notice something unusual. Inside the nacelle, ahead of the fan blades, a ring of teal green lines the casing of the Pratt & Whitney Geared Turbofan, whether the aircraft carries the PW1100G of the A320neo family or the PW1500G of the A220. The color is consistent enough across the fleet that spotters and online aviation communities have debated its purpose for years, with explanations ranging from branding to corrosion protection.

The more convincing answers sit in materials science and maintenance practice. Two separate components contribute to the green appearance, each with its own function and its own reason for the shade it carries, and a third factor, the practical needs of the people who inspect the engines, explains why the color has persisted. Examining those components in turn clarifies how a modern geared turbofan manages noise, tip clearance, and inspection, and why a seemingly cosmetic detail reflects engineering decisions made well before the engine reaches an airline.

The broad green band lining the inner surface of the fan case is the engine’s acoustic liner, a panel built from a perforated skin bonded over a honeycomb core. The perforations admit sound waves into the cells of the honeycomb, where each cell behaves like a small resonant chamber that absorbs acoustic energy and converts a portion of it into heat. By sizing the cells and the perforated face sheet for particular frequencies, designers tune the panel to dampen the tones that dominate fan noise.

The geared architecture makes this component especially relevant. Because a reduction gearbox lets the fan turn more slowly than the turbine driving it, the engine produces a different acoustic signature from a direct-drive fan of similar size, with more of the energy at lower frequencies. Low-frequency sound is harder to absorb than high-frequency sound, since longer wavelengths need deeper cavities to dissipate effectively, which is why the liner occupies a generous stretch of the inlet. Pratt & Whitney has promoted the engine’s reduced noise footprint as a headline benefit, and the liner is one of several features that contribute to it alongside the slower fan itself.

Construction follows a sandwich principle common to aerospace structures. A solid backing sheet closes one side of the honeycomb, and the perforated face sheet closes the other. The arrangement delivers acoustic performance with very little weight, a priority in any component carried on an engine hanging from the wing, where added mass raises fuel burn. The panels are also designed to withstand airflow, vibration, temperature swings, and minor debris impacts throughout a long service life.
Why The Color Comes From The Material, Not The Paint

The teal shade is generally attributed to the composite itself rather than to a decorative coating. According to descriptions of the construction , the resin and epoxy matrix that bind the liner’s layers carry a natural pigmentation that shows through on the finished surface. Engineers have a practical reason to avoid covering it. A thick film of paint would partially fill the microscopic perforations in the face sheet, reducing the open area through which sound enters the cavities and degrading the attenuation the panel was designed to achieve.

However, this explanation should be treated with some caution, because there has not been a published manufacturer statement regarding the color. As a result, the exact origin of the hue remains an informed inference rather than a documented fact. The uniform result across A320neo and A220 installations nonetheless suggests a controlled material choice instead of an incidental one.

Directly aft of the acoustic ring sits a slightly lighter blue-green band, the abradable rub strip, which technical literature also calls a fan outer air seal. Its job is to control the gap between the fan blade tips and the surrounding case. Any air that leaks across that gap represents lost work, so engine makers want the clearance as small as practical without allowing the blades to strike a hard surface.

The abradable material solves that problem by being softer than the blade tips. During break-in, the tips cut a shallow groove into the strip, producing a seal matched to the actual shape of that particular fan, including any slight growth caused by heat and centrifugal loading. The strip wears while the blades and the case remain intact. A paper from the 2003 NASA Seal/Secondary Air System Workshop , which covers Pratt & Whitney abradable seals, documents the broader engineering approach behind such materials.

The color of this strip carries its own explanation. The compound is supplied as a two-part epoxy and hardener, and the components are mixed to a defined turquoise shade so that a uniform color confirms the two parts were blended properly before application. Streaks or patches of a different tone would signal incomplete mixing, and with it a risk that the cured strip will not abrade predictably. The compound’s behavior over time matters as much as its initial performance. As the engine accumulates cycles, the strip gradually erodes from airflow, particles, and repeated light contact, and clearance grows accordingly. Operators therefore monitor the condition of the strip during scheduled inspections and restore it when wear exceeds published limits, a process that depends on repeating the same mixing and curing steps, and the same color check, each time the material is applied.

Beyond material chemistry, the saturated green interior gives maintenance crews a practical advantage during walk-around checks. The fan case sits in a shadowed cavity, and the blades, the hub, and any dark residue around the casing can blend together in poor light. A bright, uniform background makes departures from normal appearance easier to see.

Ramp inspectors look for several conditions in this region. Foreign object debris, such as fragments of tire, packing material, or bird remains, stands out against the green surface. Erosion of the liner or the rub strip shows as lighter patches or exposed honeycomb, and abnormal wear on the blade tips appears as unusual rub patterns where the strip has been cut. Because these checks often occur between flights under airport lighting and on tight schedules, a background that makes anomalies obvious reduces the chance of a missed finding.
body_zh: Jack 带着对航空一切事物的终生兴趣加入了 Simple Flying。他拥有佐治亚理工学院的航空航天工程学位，并且是一名经过认证的私人和远程飞行员。除了这些经验之外，杰克还曾在公司飞行部门工作过，在那里他获得了公务航空领域的第一手经验。目前，杰克在专业服务行业工作，并在工作之外继续增加飞行时间。
登上空客 A320neo 或 A220 的乘客从登机桥看发动机进气口时，通常会发现一些异常情况。在发动机舱内部，风扇叶片前面，普惠齿轮涡轮风扇发动机的外壳上有一圈青色环，无论飞机搭载的是 A320neo 系列的 PW1100G 还是 A220 的 PW1500G。整个机队的颜色足够一致，以至于观察者和在线航空社区多年来一直争论其用途，解释范围从品牌到腐蚀防护。
更令人信服的答案在于材料科学和维护实践。两个独立的成分促成了绿色外观，每个成分都有自己的功能和其所具有的色调的原因，第三个因素，即检查发动机的人员的实际需求，解释了为什么这种颜色一直存在。通过检查这些部件，可以清楚地了解现代齿轮涡轮风扇发动机如何管理噪声、叶尖间隙和检查，以及为什么看似美观的细节反映了在发动机到达航空公司之前就做出的工程决策。
风扇箱内表面衬里的宽绿色带是发动机的声学衬里，这是一个由粘合在蜂窝芯上的穿孔蒙皮制成的面板。穿孔允许声波进入蜂窝的细胞，其中每个细胞的行为就像一个小谐振室，吸收声能并将其一部分转化为热量。通过根据特定频率调整单元和穿孔面​​板的尺寸，设计人员可以调整面板以抑制主导风扇噪音的音调。
齿轮架构使得该组件特别重要。由于减速齿轮箱使风扇转动得比驱动它的涡轮更慢，因此发动机产生的声学特征与尺寸相似的直接驱动风扇不同，在较低频率下具有更多能量。低频声音比高频声音更难吸收，因为较长的波长需要更深的空腔才能有效消散，这就是衬里占据入口大部分的原因。普惠公司将发动机降低噪音足迹作为一项主要优势，而衬套是与较慢的风扇本身一起做出贡献的几个功能之一。
构造遵循航空航天结构常见的夹层原理。实心背板封闭蜂窝的一侧，穿孔面板封闭另一侧。这种布置以极轻的重量提供了声学性能，这对于悬挂在机翼上的发动机上的任何部件来说都是一个优先事项，增加的质量会增加燃油消耗。这些面板的设计还能够在较长的使用寿命内承受气流、振动、温度波动和轻微碎片的影响。
为什么颜色来自材料，而不是油漆
青色色调通常归因于复合材料本身，而不是装饰涂层。根据结构描述，粘合内衬各层的树脂和环氧树脂基体带有天然色素，可在成品表面上显现出来。工程师有一个实际的理由避免覆盖它。厚厚的油漆膜会部分填充面板上的微小穿孔，减少声音进入空腔的开放面积，并降低面板设计达到的衰减效果。
然而，这种解释应该谨慎对待，因为制造商尚未发布有关颜色的声明。因此，色调的确切起源仍然是一种有根据的推论，而不是有记录的事实。尽管如此，A320neo 和 A220 安装的统一结果表明材料选择是受控的，而不是偶然的。
声环的正后方有一个稍浅的蓝绿色带，即耐磨摩擦条，技术文献也将其称为风扇外部空气密封。它的作用是控制风扇叶片尖端与周围外壳之间的间隙。任何从该间隙泄漏的空气都会导致工作损失，因此发动机制造商希望间隙尽可能小，同时又不允许叶片撞击坚硬的表面。
可磨耗材料通过比叶片尖端更软来解决这个问题。在磨合过程中，尖端在条带上切出一个浅槽，产生与该特定风扇的实际形状相匹配的密封，包括由热和离心载荷引起的任何轻微增长。条带磨损，而刀片和外壳保持完好。 2003 年 NASA 密封/二次空气系统研讨会的一篇论文涵盖了 Pratt & Whitney 可磨耗密封件，记录了此类材料背后更广泛的工程方法。

这条条带的颜色有它自己的解释。该化合物以环氧树脂和硬化剂的两部分形式提供，并将各组分混合成规定的青绿色色调，以便均匀的颜色确认两部分在应用前已正确混合。不同色调的条纹或斑块将表明混合不完全，并且存在固化条无法按预期磨损的风险。该化合物随时间的变化与其初始性能一样重要。随着发动机循环的累积，条带逐渐受到气流、颗粒和反复轻接触的侵蚀，间隙相应增大。因此，操作员在定期检查期间监控带材的状况，并在磨损超过公布的限制时将其恢复，这一过程依赖于每次应用材料时重复相同的混合和固化步骤以及相同的颜色检查。
除了材料化学之外，饱和的绿色内饰还为维护人员在巡视检查时提供了实际优势。风扇外壳位于一个阴影空腔中，叶片、轮毂以及外壳周围的任何黑色残留物在光线不足的情况下都会混合在一起。明亮、均匀的背景使与正常外观的偏差更容易被看到。
坡道检查员会检查该地区的一些情况。轮胎碎片、包装材料或鸟类遗骸等异物碎片在绿色表面上显得格外突出。衬里或摩擦条的侵蚀表现为较浅的斑块或暴露的蜂窝，并且刀片尖端上的异常磨损表现为条带被切割处的不寻常的摩擦图案。由于这些检查通常在机场照明下且时间紧迫的航班之间进行，因此使异常现象变得明显的背景可以减少遗漏发现的可能性。

title_en: Why JSX Just Bought New Pacific Airlines, The Strange, Failed 757 Startup
title_zh: 为什么 JSX 刚刚收购了新的太平洋航空​​公司，奇怪的是，失败的 757 启动
summary: JSX has acquired failed 757 startup New Pacific Airlines, and the move looks less like a comeback than a cheap way to get a Part 121 certificate.
summary_zh: JSX 收购了失败的 757 初创公司新太平洋航空​​ (New Pacific Airlines)，此举看起来不像是东山再起，而更像是获得第 121 部分证书的廉价方式。
body_en: Public charter air carrier JSX has just acquired New Pacific Airlines, and with this, New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights, with Embraer E145 aircraft.

If you’re not familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “huh?” If you are familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “WTF?” There’s a sneaky and logical explanation here, so let me explain.
JSX acquires New Pacific Airlines, an unusual move
Let’s start with a little context. JSX is a public charter air carrier, which operates a fleet of nearly 60 planes, most of which are Embraer E135s and E145s.

It operates as a Part 135 operator, meaning it’s not technically an airline, as it’s using a loophole that allows it to not use standard TSA security screening, hire pilots with fewer than 1,500 hours, etc. Basically what’s happening is that one subsidiary sells the tickets, and then another subsidiary operates the flights, so it’s technically a “charter” (with 30 people who don’t know one another).

Then there’s New Pacific Airlines, one of the strangest airline startups we’ve ever seen, and which I’ve covered extensively. The airline acquired some Boeing 757s, and the business plan was to connect North America and Asia via Anchorage (ANC).

The business model made zero sense in the first place, though there was some funding there, and they even invested in constructing a lounge in Anchorage, even though those flights never did happen. The airline did briefly fly from (ONT) to Nashville (BNA) — as one does — before ultimately going out of business .

That brings us to the news. New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights with Embraer E145s that are leased from JSX, as reported by IshrionA . According to a Department of Transportation filing , the airline intends to resume flights with planes featuring 42 seats, which is higher than the 30-seat limit you’ll find on current JSX planes.
New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights with ERJ 145 leased from JSX. pic.twitter.com/uMMS0J2fZy
Ishrion Aviation (@IshrionA) November 20, 2026
This really appears to be a (smart) Part 121 play
On the surface, this of course makes absolutely no sense. New Pacific Airlines was out of business, and the business model made no sense. So why would JSX buy an airline and then lease planes to it?

Long story short, this seems to be a play to acquire a cheap Part 121 certificate. A Part 121 operator is a company that’s allowed to operate scheduled air transport… in other words, a “real” airline. As I mentioned above, JSX has historically been a Part 135 operator, and that explicitly means it’s not an airline. It’s a public charter air carrier, so it’s not a “real” airline.

Going back a couple of years, we know that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) was considering cracking down on carriers like JSX , since they definitely don’t operate within the spirit of the rules. That’s not to say that JSX did anything wrong, because by the letter of the law, they’re following it exactly. It’s just that the letter of the law makes no sense, and clearly doesn’t reflect the intent behind distinguishing between Part 121 and Part 135 operators.

Under Trump, there was no scrutiny of this. However, with Democrats soon controlling both the House and Senate, I imagine JSX leaders may be worried that there could again be more scrutiny. If nothing else, buying a cheap Part 121 certificate is a good insurance policy, in case the government does crack down. After all, these can basically be “sold,” while acquiring one from scratch can be grueling process.

I wouldn’t assume that anything will really operate with New Pacific Airlines branding, or based on a New Pacific Airlines business model. Instead, I imagine the idea is that JSX will start dabbling in Part 121 operations, which is why these planes will have more seats (above the 30-seat cap that’s allowed), since that’s no longer a factor.

If the government were to crack down on Part 135 operators, JSX could move to Part 121 operations. However, they’d have to make lots of changes, from their pilot hiring, to the way passengers are screened.

JSX has just bought New Pacific, the airline with an absurd business model that went bankrupt. No, JSX isn’t inspired by the concept of flying Boeing 757s to Asia. Instead, this is clearly the cheapest way for JSX to acquire a Part 121 certificate, which would be required for the carrier to continue operations in the event that the government were to crack down on the Part 135 operator loophole.

It’s going to be interesting to see how this evolves, both since JSX seems to have plans to operate Part 121 operations in the near future, and also to see how JSX’s business model would evolve if the Part 135 concept were blocked.
body_zh: 公共包机航空公司 JSX 刚刚收购了新太平洋航空​​，新太平洋航空​​打算恢复使用巴西航空工业公司 E145 飞机的航班。
如果您不熟悉新太平洋航空​​公司，您可能会想“啊？”如果您熟悉新太平洋航空​​公司，您可能会想“WTF？”这里有一个偷偷摸摸且合乎逻辑的解释，所以让我解释一下。
JSX 收购新太平洋航空​​公司，这是一个不寻常的举动
让我们从一些背景开始。 JSX 是一家公共包机航空公司，运营着近 60 架飞机的机队，其中大部分是巴西航空工业公司 E135 和 E145。
它以 Part 135 运营商的身份运营，这意味着从技术上讲它不是一家航空公司，因为它利用了一个漏洞，使其无法使用标准的 TSA 安检、雇用飞行时间少于 1,500 小时的飞行员等。基本上发生的情况是，一家子公司出售机票，然后另一家子公司运营航班，因此从技术上讲，它是一种“包机”（有 30 名彼此不认识的人）。
然后是新太平洋航空​​公司，这是我们见过的最奇怪的航空公司初创公司之一，我对此进行了广泛的报道。该航空公司购买了一些波音 757，其商业计划是通过安克雷奇 (ANC) 连接北美和亚洲。
这种商业模式一开始就毫无意义，尽管那里有一些资金，他们甚至投资在安克雷奇建造一个休息室，尽管这些航班从未发生过。该航空公司确实曾短暂运营过从 (ONT) 飞往纳什维尔 (BNA) 的航班（正如航空公司所做的那样），但最终停业。
这给我们带来了新闻。据 IshrionA 报道，新太平洋航空​​公司打算恢复使用从 JSX 租赁的巴西航空工业公司 E145 飞机的航班。根据运输部的一份文件，该航空公司打算恢复 42 座飞机的航班，这高于当前 JSX 飞机的 30 座限制。
新太平洋航空​​打算恢复使用从 JSX 租赁的 ERJ 145 的航班。 pic.twitter.com/uMMS0J2fZy
Ishrion 航空 (@IhrionA) 2026 年 11 月 20 日
这看起来确实是一部（聪明的）第121部剧
从表面上看，这当然毫无意义。新太平洋航空​​公司破产了，其商业模式毫无意义。那么，JSX 为什么要收购一家航空公司，然后向其租赁飞机呢？
长话短说，这似乎是为了获得廉价的 Part 121 证书而进行的游戏。第 121 部分运营商是一家获准运营定期航空运输的公司……换句话说，是一家“真正的”航空公司。正如我上面提到的，JSX 历来都是 Part 135 运营商，这明确意味着它不是一家航空公司。它是一家公共包机航空公司，所以它不是一家“真正的”航空公司。
回溯几年，我们知道美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 正在考虑打击 JSX 等航空公司，因为它们绝对不符合规则精神。这并不是说 JSX 做错了什么，因为根据法律条文，他们是严格遵守的。只是法律条文毫无意义，并且显然没有反映出区分第 121 部分和第 135 部分运营商背后的意图。
在特朗普的领导下，对此没有任何审查。然而，随着民主党很快控制众议院和参议院，我想 JSX 领导人可能会担心可能会再次受到更多审查。如果不出意外的话，购买便宜的第 121 部分证书是一项很好的保险政策，以防政府严厉打击。毕竟，这些基本上可以“出售”，而从头开始获取一个可能是一个艰苦的过程。
我不认为任何东西都会真正以新太平洋航空​​品牌运作，或基于新太平洋航空​​商业模式。相反，我认为 JSX 将开始涉足第 121 部分的运营，这就是为什么这些飞机将拥有更多座位（超过允许的 30 座上限），因为这不再是一个因素。
如果政府要打击第 135 部分运营商，JSX 可能会转向第 121 部分运营。然而，他们必须做出很多改变，从飞行员的招聘到乘客的筛查方式。
JSX 刚刚收购了新太平洋航空​​公司，这家商业模式荒唐的航空公司已经破产。不，JSX 的灵感并非来自波音 757 飞往亚洲的概念。相反，这显然是 JSX 获得 Part 121 证书的最便宜的方式，如果政府要打击 Part 135 运营商漏洞，承运商将需要该证书才能继续运营。
看看这种情况如何发展将会很有趣，因为 JSX 似乎计划在不久的将来运营第 121 部分业务，而且还想看看如果第 135 部分概念被阻止，JSX 的商业模式将如何发展。

title_en: Is It True That The Boeing 747-8 & 787 Dreamliner Are Powered By The Same Engine?
title_zh: 波音 747-8 和 787 梦想飞机真的由同一台发动机提供动力吗？
summary: Comparing and contrasting two leading American widebodies.
summary_zh: 比较和对比两种领先的美国宽体飞机。
body_en: Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

It is true that both the 747-8, the final iteration of the Boeing double-decker, and the 787 Dreamliner, its latest and greatest clean sheet design, use the same engine. However, each of these aircraft uses a different variation of that same turbofan that is tailored to its unique needs and engineering qualities.

The 747-8 exclusively uses the GEnx-2B while the 787 Dreamliner is the only jetliner to ever be equipped with the GEnx-1B. Boeing chose the GEnx for the 747-8 primarily to modernize the aging jumbo jet with next-generation technology. Both aircraft feature distinctive serrated chevrons on the engine nacelles, which mix hot exhaust with cool air to significantly reduce noise.

For airlines that operate both the 787 and 747-8, using the same engine family simplifies maintenance, parts inventory, and technician training. The GEnx-1B is a larger, more powerful, and more-electric engine designed for a modern twin-engine jet. The GEnx-2B is a smaller, simplified variant that incorporates traditional pneumatics to breathe life into the older 747 systems while providing modern fuel efficiency.

While the GEnx-1B (787) and GEnx-2B (747-8) share a common high-pressure core and 80% of their Line Replaceable Units, they are distinct engines optimized for different aircraft architectures. The most fundamental difference is how the engines interact with the aircraft's internal systems. The GEnx family is designed to stay on wing 20% longer than previous generations, with some fleet leaders exceeding 30,000 hours without a major overhaul.

Both engines offer approximately 15% better fuel efficiency than the older CF6 engines they replaced. Tom Levin, General Manager of the GEnx/CF6 engine product line at GE Aviation, commented on the engine's success when the 1,000th GEnx engine was developed in 2015.

“The GEnx was the fastest selling engine in GE’s history, and now it is the fastest production ramp up of a GE widebody engine program. The GEnx engine has proven itself with outstanding performance and reliability."

The 787 uses a bleedless architecture where most systems are powered electrically. The 747-8 uses a traditional bleed-air system to power environmental controls and start the engines, requiring the GEnx-2B to include bleed-air ports. The GEnx-2B has fewer stages in the booster and low-pressure turbine, optimizing it for a four-engine configuration.

The Boeing 747-8, on the other hand, uses a traditional bleed air system. It must bleed high-pressure air from the compressor to power the 747’s pneumatic systems, including cabin pressurization and thermal anti-icing.

To fit the 747’s wing and ground clearance, the GEnx-2B has a smaller fan diameter, 105 inches, compared to the 787’s 111 inches. Because the 747-8 has four engines while the 787 has only two, the -2B is simplified internally to be lighter and more optimized for its lower per-engine thrust requirement. The -2B produces roughly 66,500 lbs of thrust, whereas the 787 variants can reach up to 76,100 lbs.

The GEnx-1B has more power because it is intended for a twin-engine aircraft (787) that must maintain performance in the event of an engine failure during takeoff. Because the GEnx-2B's power is distributed across four engines on the 747-8, its thrust rating is 66,500 lbf lower. Compared with older engines like the CF6, the GEnx-2B's technology improves fuel efficiency and cuts emissions by 15%.

In contrast to the 1B, the GEnx-2B has de-staged components to maximize weight and performance for a four-engine setup. In contrast to the 1B's four stages, the 2B's low-pressure compressor has three stages. In the low-pressure turbine, the 1B has seven stages, whereas the 2B has six.

Compared with the 747-8 , the 787 Dreamliner delivers better economics and is much more efficient in the widebody market, as it is a lightweight twin-engine composite aircraft. These engineering variations determine their efficiency and commercial success. The 747 uses about 3,800 gallons of fuel per hour, while the 787 uses about 2,900 gallons. The 787-9 is extremely efficient, using approximately 2.31 liters per 100 km per passenger, which is significantly better than the 747-8's 2.82 liters per 100 km per passenger.

Boeing's Dreamliner also costs significantly less to operate, with a lower cost per available seat mile. Airlines typically prefer smaller twin-engine aircraft because they are less dangerous to fill and fly. The 787's design and performance have allowed it to thrive in the modern aviation market, while the 747-8 saw limited passenger orders before production ended in 2017 and the 747 assembly line fully shut down in 2023.

The Dreamliner has essentially eliminated the conventional hub-and-spoke paradigm that made the 747 necessary. While the 747 required high passenger capacity to be successful, the 787's efficiency lets it cover the same distances with fewer seats, making it a better match for today's point-to-point market.

The 787's efficiency allows airlines to launch new, nonstop point-to-point routes that would not have been economically viable with older, bigger, four-engine planes. Despite being more efficient than previous 747s, the 747-8 is still best suited to high-volume hub-to-hub services. Airlines such as United have made large 787 orders to replace a mix of 747s, 767s, and early 777s with a single, simpler aircraft family, resulting in significant cost savings for pilot training and component inventory.

The 787 incorporates a large amount of carbon composite material, making it lighter, more resistant to fatigue and corrosion, and allowing for higher cabin humidity and lower cabin altitude, which enhances passenger comfort and reduces structural stress. The 747-8 is a development of a traditional aluminum design, with a heavier base structure.

Lufthansa has incorporated the 787-9 to handle flights that need the same range but have about 70–90 fewer people, even though it is still a 747-8 operator. Because of this, even at off-peak times, the airline can maintain high load factors (percentage of seats filled). British Airways switched to the 787-10 for important transatlantic flights to New York and Chicago after retiring its entire 747 fleet. The 787-10 is 25% more fuel-efficient than the 747 while offering comparable cargo capacity and contemporary comforts.
body_zh: 卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
确实，波音双层客机的最终版本 747-8 和最新、最出色的全新设计 787 梦想飞机都使用相同的发动机。然而，每架飞机都使用同一涡轮风扇的不同变体，这些变体是根据其独特的需求和工程质量量身定制的。
747-8 专门使用 GEnx-2B，而 787 梦想飞机是唯一配备 GEnx-1B 的喷气式客机。波音公司为 747-8 选择 GEnx 主要是为了利用下一代技术对老化的大型喷气式飞机进行现代化改造。这两款飞机的发动机短舱上均采用独特的锯齿状 V 形花纹，可将热废气与冷空气混合，从而显着降低噪音。
对于同时运营 787 和 747-8 的航空公司来说，使用相同的发动机系列可以简化维护、零件库存和技术人员培训。 GEnx-1B 是一款更大、更强大、更电动的发动机，专为现代双引擎喷气式飞机而设计。 GEnx-2B 是一种更小、更简化的变体，它结合了传统的气动装置，为旧的 747 系统注入活力，同时提供现代燃油效率。
虽然 GEnx-1B (787) 和 GEnx-2B (747-8) 共享一个共同的高压核心和 80% 的现场可更换单元，但它们是针对不同飞机架构优化的不同发动机。最根本的区别在于发动机与飞机内部系统的交互方式。 GEnx 系列的设计寿命比前几代机长 20%，一些领先机队在没有大修的情况下使用寿命超过 30,000 小时。
这两款发动机的燃油效率比它们所替代的旧款 CF6 发动机高出约 15%。 GE航空集团GEnx/CF6发动机产品线总经理Tom Levin在2015年开发出第1000台GEnx发动机时评论了该发动机的成功。
“GEnx 是 GE 历史上销售最快的发动机，现在它是 GE 宽体发动机项目中产量增长最快的。GEnx 发动机已经证明了自己出色的性能和可靠性。”
787 采用无泄气架构，其中大多数系统均采用电力供电。 747-8 使用传统的引气系统为环境控制提供动力并启动发动机，要求 GEnx-2B 包含引气端口。 GEnx-2B 的增压器和低压涡轮级数较少，从而针对四发动机配置进行了优化。
另一方面，波音 747-8 使用传统的引气系统。它必须从压缩机中排出高压空气，为 747 的气动系统提供动力，包括机舱增压和热防冰。
为了适应 747 的机翼和离地间隙，GEnx-2B 的风扇直径较小，为 105 英寸，而 787 的风扇直径为 111 英寸。由于 747-8 有四个发动机，而 787 只有两个发动机，因此 -2B 进行了内部简化，重量更轻，并且针对每台发动机的推力要求较低，进行了优化。 -2B 产生大约 66,500 磅的推力，而 787 型号的推力可达 76,100 磅。
GEnx-1B 具有更大的功率，因为​​它适用于双引擎飞机 (787)，在起飞过程中发生发动机故障时必须保持性能。由于 GEnx-2B 的动力分布在 747-8 上的四个发动机上，因此其额定推力降低了 66,500 磅力。与 CF6 等老式发动机相比，GEnx-2B 的技术提高了燃油效率，并将排放量减少了 15%。
与 1B 相比，GEnx-2B 取消了组件，以最大限度地提高四引擎设置的重量和性能。与 1B 的四级相比，2B 的低压压缩机具有三级。在低压涡轮机中，1B 有七级，而 2B 有六级。
与 747-8 相比，787 梦想飞机具有更好的经济性，并且在宽体市场上效率更高，因为它是一款轻型双引擎复合材料飞机。这些工程变化决定了它们的效率和商业成功。 747 每小时使用约 3,800 加仑燃油，而 787 每小时使用约 2,900 加仑燃油。 787-9 的效率极高，每位乘客每 100 公里耗油约 2.31 升，明显优于 747-8 每位乘客每 100 公里 2.82 升。
波音梦想飞机的运营成本也显着降低，每可用座位英里的成本也更低。航空公司通常更喜欢较小的双引擎飞机，因为它们填充和飞行的危险性较小。 787 的设计和性能使其在现代航空市场中蓬勃发展，而 747-8 在 2017 年停产之前的客运订单有限，747 装配线于 2023 年完全关闭。
梦想飞机基本上消除了 747 所必需的传统轮辐式模式。虽然 747 需要高载客量才能取得成功，但 787 的效率使其能够以更少的座位覆盖相同的距离，从而更适合当今的点对点市场。
787 的效率使航空公司能够开通新的、不间断的点对点航线，而使用老式、更大的四引擎飞机在经济上是不可行的。尽管比之前的 747 更加高效，747-8 仍然最适合大容量的枢纽到枢纽服务。美联航等航空公司已订购了大量 787 飞机，用单一、更简单的飞机系列取代 747、767 和早期 777 飞机，从而显着节省了飞行员培训和零部件库存的成本。
787采用大量碳复合材料，使其更轻、更耐疲劳和耐腐蚀，并允许更高的客舱湿度和更低的客舱高度，从而增强乘客舒适度并减少结构应力。 747-8 是传统铝制设计的发展，具有较重的底座结构。
汉莎航空已采用 787-9 来处理需要相同航程但载客量减少约 70-90 人的航班，尽管它仍然是 747-8 运营商。正因为如此，即使在非高峰时段，航空公司也能保持较高的载客率（座位满座率）。英国航空在退役其整个 747 机队后，改用 787-10 执飞飞往纽约和芝加哥的重要跨大西洋航班。 787-10 的燃油效率比 747 高 25%，同时提供可比的载货能力和现代舒适性。

title_en: Here's How Much The 787 Dreamliner Heavily Influenced Boeing's 747-8 Development
title_zh: 787 梦想飞机对波音 747-8 开发的影响有多大
summary: The 787 and 747-8 represent a distinct moment in Boeing manufacturing history.
summary_zh: 787 和 747-8 代表了波音制造史上的一个独特时刻。
body_en: Jack comes to Simple Flying with a lifelong interest in all things aviation. He holds a degree in Aerospace Engineering from Georgia Tech, and is a certified private and remote pilot. Beyond these experiences, Jack previously worked for a corporate flight department where he gained first-hand experience in the world of business aviation. Currently, Jack works in the professional services industry and continues to build his flight hours outside of work.

When Boeing launched the 747-8 in November 2005, it presented the airplane as a stretched, re-winged, and re-engined update of the 747-400 that would use technology borrowed from the 787 Dreamliner . The Dreamliner program had been launched only a year earlier, and its work on lightweight composites, efficient engines, and electronically managed systems gave Boeing a supply of proven solutions at the moment the aging jumbo needed them.

Rather than commissioning an all-new quadjet for a limited market, Boeing chose to graft selected Dreamliner innovations onto a familiar airframe, which kept development costs manageable and preserved the operating familiarity that long-time 747 customers valued. The resulting aircraft differs from its predecessor in several visible ways, yet it remains a 747 in its structure and in the way it is flown, so a fair assessment of the Dreamliner’s influence requires examining each major system in turn. That review shows a program that borrowed boldly where performance was at stake and conservatively wherever certification, cost, or pilot familiarity argued for restraint.
Engines: The Dreamliner’s Most Direct Contribution

The most substantial transfer from the 787 program came through the powerplants. The 747-8 uses four General Electric GEnx-2B67 engines , a smaller-diameter relative of the GEnx developed for the Dreamliner. The design emphasizes a high bypass ratio, sending most of the air around the core to generate thrust more efficiently than the lower-bypass engines of earlier generations.

Engineers modified the design so that each engine could supply bleed air, the compressed air tapped from the engine to run onboard systems, because the 747 still depends on a conventional pneumatic architecture that the 787 largely abandoned in favor of electrical power . Each engine generates 66,500 pounds (30,164 kg) of thrust and carries a 105-inch (267 cm) composite fan, a material choice that cuts weight relative to metallic blades.

Sawtooth-shaped edges called chevrons line the rear of the engine housing, borrowing a noise-reduction device from the 787 that encourages exhaust and bypass air to blend more gradually. Noise also carries financial weight, since many airports levy charges tied to certified noise levels, and Boeing has said the 747-8 produces a considerably smaller noise footprint than the 747-400.

Sharing a design lineage with the 787 engine allowed Boeing and GE to spread development effort across two programs rather than funding a bespoke powerplant for a model expected to sell in modest numbers. Unlike the Dreamliner, which Boeing offers with a choice between GE and Rolls-Royce engines, the 747-8 is offered only with the GEnx-2B, which spared Boeing the cost of certifying a second powerplant for a modest order book. For operators, the engine change translated into lower fuel burn and emissions per seat than the 747-400, which formed the core of the airplane’s commercial pitch to airlines and cargo carriers.

Boeing designed a new wing for the 747-8 with fresh airfoil shapes intended to improve aerodynamic efficiency at cruise. Designing a wing for a derivative airplane also imposes constraints that a clean-sheet program avoids, because the new surface had to mate with the existing fuselage architecture, which limited how far the planform could depart from the 747-400’s.

At the tips, the upright winglets of the 747-400 gave way to raked wingtips, the same approach used on the 777 and the 787. Sweeping the tip aft reduces drag generated by wingtip vortices while adding less weight than a taller vertical surface would. The configuration debuted on the 767-400ER, which means the 747-8 inherited it from a lineage broader than the Dreamliner alone.

Boeing attributes the 747-8’s higher cruising speed relative to the 747-400 to the combined effect of the wing, wingtips, and engines. The gain matters to passenger carriers flying long routes, where minutes accumulate into meaningful time savings. The aerodynamic gains in cruise efficiency also translate directly into range or payload, which matters especially for the freighter, where operators trade fuel against cargo on long sectors.

The larger wing extends the span to roughly 224 feet (68.27 meters), compared with about 211 feet (64.31 meters) on the 747-400, a growth that supports the airplane’s higher maximum takeoff weight. Aerodynamic refinement of this kind typically yields incremental gains, yet on an airplane that burns many tons of fuel on every long flight, even small improvements compound into sizable savings over a fleet’s life.
Flight Controls And Cockpit: Modernization With Restraint

The 747-8 also adopted elements of the 787’s fly-by-wire philosophy , in which pilot inputs travel as electrical signals to flight control computers rather than moving surfaces through mechanical cables and pulleys. Electronic signaling reduces weight, since cable runs and associated hardware can be shortened, and it allows computers to modulate surface movements for smoother handling and greater structural efficiency.

The shift follows a broader pattern within the company, since the 777 was Boeing’s first fly-by-wire airliner and the 787 extended that approach more thoroughly. Boeing applied the technology selectively because it wanted qualified pilots on the 747-400 to move to the new model easily. The flight deck therefore keeps a layout and control feel close to its predecessor’s.

Training pilots on an unfamiliar type requires simulator time, instructor capacity, and revenue flying hours that airlines would rather devote to scheduled service, so commonality functions as a quiet but substantial financial benefit for operators already flying the 747-400, whose crews can serve both types. The Dreamliner, by contrast, was free to adopt an entirely new flight deck, a freedom the 747-8 deliberately did not exercise.
The Cabin: Dreamliner Atmosphere On A Familiar Frame
body_zh: Jack 带着对航空一切事物的终生兴趣加入了 Simple Flying。他拥有佐治亚理工学院的航空航天工程学位，并且是一名经过认证的私人和远程飞行员。除了这些经验之外，杰克还曾在公司飞行部门工作过，在那里他获得了公务航空领域的第一手经验。目前，杰克在专业服务行业工作，并在工作之外继续增加飞行时间。
当波音公司于 2005 年 11 月推出 747-8 时，该飞机是 747-400 的加长、重新机翼和重新发动机的升级版，将使用借自 787 梦想飞机的技术。梦想客机项目仅在一年前启动，其在轻质复合材料、高效发动机和电子管理系统方面的工作为波音公司提供了经过验证的解决方案，以应对这架老化的大型飞机的需要。

波音没有为有限的市场调试全新的四轴喷气式飞机，而是选择将选定的梦想客机创新技术移植到熟悉的机身上，这使得开发成本易于管理，并保留了 747 长期客户所看重的操作熟悉度。由此产生的飞机在几个明显的方面与其前身有所不同，但其结构和飞行方式仍然是 747，因此要公平评估梦想飞机的影响力需要依次检查每个主要系统。该审查表明，该计划在性能受到威胁的地方大胆借鉴，而在认证、成本或飞行员熟悉度要求限制的地方则保守地借鉴。
发动机：梦想飞机最直接的贡献
787 项目最重要的转变来自于动力装置。 747-8 使用四台通用电气 GEnx-2B67 发动机，这是为梦想客机开发的 GEnx 的较小直径发动机。该设计强调高涵道比，将大部分空气输送到核心周围，从而比前几代低涵道比发动机更有效地产生推力。
工程师修改了设计，以便每台发动机都可以提供引气，即从发动机排出的压缩空气来运行机载系统，因为 747 仍然依赖于传统的气动架构，787 基本上放弃了这种架构，转而采用电力。每台发动机可产生 66,500 磅（30,164 千克）的推力，并带有一个 105 英寸（267 厘米）的复合材料风扇，这种材料选择相对于金属叶片可以减轻重量。
发动机外壳后部排列着称为“人字形”的锯齿形边缘，借用了 787 的降噪装置，可促进排气和旁通空气逐渐混合。噪音还具有财务影响力，因为许多机场都会根据经过认证的噪音水平收取费用，波音公司表示，747-8 产生的噪音足迹比 747-400 小得多。

与 787 发动机共享设计血统，使波音和通用电气能够将开发工作分散到两个项目中，而不是为预计销量不大的机型提供定制动力装置。与梦想客机不同的是，波音公司提供 GE 和劳斯莱斯发动机可供选择，而 747-8 则只提供 GEnx-2B，这使得波音公司无需花费少量的订单来认证第二个动力装置。对于运营商来说，发动机的改变意味着比 747-400 更低的每座燃油消耗和排放，而 747-400 构成了该飞机向航空公司和货运公司进行商业宣传的核心。
波音公司为 747-8 设计了新机翼，其翼型形状新颖，旨在提高巡航时的空气动力效率。为衍生飞机设计机翼还施加了清洁计划要避免的限制，因为新的表面必须与现有的机身架构相匹配，这限制了平面形状与 747-400 的偏离程度。
在翼尖处，747-400 的直立小翼让位于倾斜翼尖，这与 777 和 787 上使用的方法相同。向后扫翼尖可减少翼尖涡流产生的阻力，同时比较高的垂直表面增加的重量更少。该配置首次在 767-400ER 上首次亮相，这意味着 747-8 继承了比梦想飞机更广泛的血统。
波音公司将 747-8 相对于 747-400 更高的巡航速度归因于机翼、翼尖和发动机的综合作用。对于长途航线的客运航空公司来说，这一收益很重要，因为在这些航线上，时间的积累可以节省大量的时间。巡航效率的空气动力学收益也直接转化为航程或有效载荷，这对于货船尤其重要，因为运营商在长航段上用燃料与货物进行贸易。
较大的机翼将翼展扩展至约 224 英尺（68.27 米），而 747-400 的翼展约为 211 英尺（64.31 米），这一增长支持了飞机更高的最大起飞重量。这种空气动力学改进通常会带来增量收益，但对于每次长途飞行都会燃烧大量燃油的飞机来说，即使是很小的改进，也会在机队的使用寿命内节省大量成本。
飞行控制和驾驶舱：有约束的现代化
747-8 还采用了 787 电传操纵原理的元素，其中飞行员输入作为电信号传输到飞行控制计算机，而不是通过机械电缆和滑轮移动表面。电子信号减轻了重量，因为电缆线路和相关硬件可以缩短，并且它允许计算机调节表面运动，以实现更平稳的操作和更高的结构效率。
这一转变遵循了公司内部更广泛的模式，因为 777 是波音第一架电传操纵客机，而 787 则更彻底地扩展了这种方法。波音公司有选择地应用了该技术，因为它希望 747-400 上合格的飞行员能够轻松过渡到新型号。因此，驾驶舱的布局和控制感与其前身相似。
培训飞行员使用不熟悉的机型需要模拟器时间、教员能力和收入飞行时间，而航空公司宁愿将这些时间投入到定期服务中，因此对于已经驾驶 747-400 的运营商来说，通用性可以带来安静但可观的经济效益，因为其机组人员可以为这两种机型提供服务。相比之下，梦想飞机可以自由地采用全新的飞行甲板，而 747-8 则故意不行使这种自由。
