title_en: Mexico’s President Flew 21 Hours To China In Economy (In A Middle Seat!)
title_zh: 墨西哥总统乘坐经济舱飞了21个小时来到中国（坐中间座位！）
summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum reportedly flew China Southern economy, in a middle seat, on a 21-hour trip to the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with a refueling stop in Tijuana.
summary_zh: 据报道，墨西哥总统克劳迪娅·辛鲍姆乘坐南航经济舱中座飞机，在21小时的深圳APEC峰会之旅中乘坐了南航经济舱飞机。
body_en: I’ve gotta say, huge kudos to Mexico’s President, Claudia Sheinbaum, for setting quite the example in terms of how she recently traveled to China, as flagged by View from the Wing …
Claudia Sheinbaum flies China Southern economy to Shenzhen

World leaders have just met in Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting. As you’d expect, most leaders flew on their government planes. There were some exceptions, though I can’t imagine anyone else flew the same way as Mexico’s 64-year-old president.
Viajamos hacia Shenzhen para representar a México en el Foro de Cooperación Económica Asia-Pacífico (APEC) China 2026; la agenda de actividades incluye reunión con empresarios de países miembros.
Además, participaré en la conferencia de prensa matutina para informar avances de… pic.twitter.com/F9UqRLjFlb
Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) November 15, 2026

Media reports suggest she flew to China on China Southern. Specifically, she traveled on Sunday, November 15, 2026, on CZ8032, from Mexico City (MEX) to Shenzhen (SZX), with a refueling stop in Tijuana (TIJ), and the journey covering a distance of 8,803 miles.

The Airbus A350-900 took off from Mexico City at 12:49AM, arriving in Tijuana at 2:02AM, after a flight time of 3hr13min. Then it took off again at 4:34AM, and landed in Shenzhen the following morning at 11:31AM, after a flight time of 14hr56min. All-in-all, the flight took around 21 hours, including the refueling stop.
The shocking thing here isn’t that she traveled commercial, but instead, that she reportedly flew in economy! Reports suggest she was in seat 33B, which would be a middle seat in economy, no less!
Llegamos a la Ciudad de México en el vuelo CZ8031 desde Shenzhen, China. Agradecemos a toda la tripulación por su apoyo. pic.twitter.com/DSC83CpnDQ
Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) November 20, 2026
That’s probably unnecessary, but sets a nice example!
I think a head of state should reasonably be able to fly business class on a flight of this length, for two reasons
She has important work to do at a summit like this, and there’s value in her being well rested when she arrives; there’s simply no denying that you can rest better if you have a flat bed
She could be more productive during the flight if she had space to work on things, as comfort does make a difference with productivity

That being said, I absolutely commend her for the example she is setting. It’s certainly quite a contrast to what we’ve seen here, where President Trump accepted a Boeing 747-8 as a gift from Qatar, and talked about how he has done it to make Americans be proud , because “our country has to be represented properly.” Heck, just this week he talked about “China was very impressed” and “Russia was very impressed” of his new plane. Lovely, I’m happy we’re impressing Putin, that makes me proud to be an American!

"Russia was very impressed" — Trump leads his press conference by bragging about taking the longest flight in Air Force One history, in case you were worried that he actually accomplished something useful on his trip pic.twitter.com/dDIHg8wb1w

Keep in mind that Mexico has an interesting history when it comes to how leaders fly. In 2016, Mexico’s government took control of a private Boeing 787, which flew around former President Enrique Pena Nieto. The purchase of the plane had actually been arranged under the previous president, Felipe Calderón, in 2012.

Then in 2018, when Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador took charge in Mexico, he fulfilled a campaign promise of selling that 787, which turned out to be pretty challenging, given that demand for a secondhand VIP 787 isn’t exactly that high (the plane ended up going to Tajikistan). Sheinbaum has kept that general legacy going, by flying commercial.

Mexico’s President, Claudia Sheinbaum, traveled to the recent summit in China differently than virtually all other government leaders. Not only did she fly commercial, but she traveled in economy, and reportedly even in a middle seat.
body_zh: 我不得不说，墨西哥总统克劳迪娅·谢因鲍姆（Claudia Sheinbaum）在她最近前往中国的方式方面树立了榜样，正如《View from the Wing》所指出的那样……
Claudia Sheinbaum 搭乘南航经济舱飞往深圳
世界领导人刚刚在中国深圳举行亚太经合组织（APEC）领导人非正式会议。正如你所料，大多数领导人都乘坐政府飞机。也有一些例外，但我无法想象还有其他人会以与 64 岁的墨西哥总统相同的方式飞行。
Viajamos hacia 深圳代表墨西哥参加 2026 年亚太经合组织 (APEC) 中国会议；活动议程包括与各国企业的重聚。
Además，参加会议以通知… pic.twitter.com/F9UqRLjFlb
克劳迪娅·谢因鲍姆·帕尔多 (@Claudiashein) 2026 年 11 月 15 日
媒体报道称她乘坐中国南方航空飞往中国。具体来说，她于2026年11月15日星期日乘坐CZ8032从墨西哥城（MEX）飞往深圳（SZX），并在蒂华纳（TIJ）加油，行程8,803英里。
这架空客 A350-900 于中午 12:49 从墨西哥城起飞，经过 3 小时 13 分钟的飞行时间，于凌晨 2:02 抵达蒂华纳。随后于凌晨4点34分再次起飞，经过14小时56分的飞行时间，于次日上午11点31分抵达深圳。总而言之，包括中途加油在内，飞行时间约为 21 小时。
令人震惊的不是她乘坐的是商务航班，而是据报道她乘坐的是经济舱！有报道称她坐在 33B 座位，这将是经济舱的中间座位！
Llegamos a la Ciudad de México en el vuelo CZ8031 来自中国深圳。 Agradecemos a toda la tripulación por su apoyo。 pic.twitter.com/DSC83CpnDQ
克劳迪娅·谢因鲍姆·帕尔多 (@Claudiashein) 2026 年 11 月 20 日
这可能是不必要的，但树立了一个很好的榜样！
我认为国家元首应该能够在这么长的航班上乘坐商务舱，原因有两个
在这样的峰会上她有重要的工作要做，到达后充分休息是很有价值的。不可否认的是，如果您有一张平坦的床，您可以休息得更好
如果她有空间处理事情，她在飞行过程中的工作效率可能会更高，因为舒适度确实会提高工作效率
话虽这么说，我绝对赞扬她所树立的榜样。这当然与我们在这里看到的形成鲜明对比，特朗普总统接受了卡塔尔赠送的一架波音 747-8 飞机，并谈到他如何做到这一点，让美国人感到自豪，因为“我们的国家必须得到适当的代表”。哎呀，就在本周，他谈到了他的新飞机“中国印象深刻”和“俄罗斯印象深刻”。可爱的是，我很高兴我们给普京留下了深刻的印象，这让我为自己是美国人而感到自豪！
“俄罗斯印象非常深刻”——特朗普在新闻发布会上吹嘘自己乘坐了空军一号历史上最长的飞行，以防你担心他在这次旅行中实际上完成了一些有用的事情 pic.twitter.com/dDIHg8wb1w
请记住，墨西哥在领导人如何飞行方面有着一段有趣的历史。 2016年，墨西哥政府控制了一架私人波音787，该飞机曾在前总统恩里克·佩纳·涅托周围飞行。这架飞机的购买实际上是在 2012 年前任总统费利佩·卡尔德龙 (Felipe Calderón) 的领导下安排的。
然后在 2018 年，当安德烈斯·曼努埃尔·洛佩兹·奥夫拉多尔 (Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador) 掌管墨西哥时，他兑现了出售这架 787 的竞选承诺，但事实证明，这相当具有挑战性，因为对二手 VIP 787 的需求并不那么高（这架飞机最终飞往塔吉克斯坦）。希恩鲍姆通过商业飞行延续了这一传统。
墨西哥总统克劳迪娅·谢因鲍姆 (Claudia Sheinbaum) 出席最近在中国举行的峰会的方式与几乎所有其他政府领导人不同。她不仅乘坐商务航班，还乘坐经济舱，据报道甚至坐在中间座位。

title_en: Aviation Gems: The Airbus A380 Is The Largest, But The Boeing 747-8 Actually Holds 2 Worldwide Titles
title_zh: 航空瑰宝：空客 A380 是最大的，但波音 747-8 实际上拥有两项全球冠军
summary: A closer look at the edge that Boeing's iconic 747 still holds over the gargantuan Airbus A380 to this day.
summary_zh: 仔细观察至今，波音标志性 747 相对于庞大的空客 A380 仍然具有的优势。
body_en: Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

The introduction of the Airbus A380 historically dethroned Boeing as the reigning champion of big jet builders. However, that statement comes with a couple of caveats. It is true that the A380 beats the classic Boeing 747 in wingspan, height, weight, and passenger capacity, but the long-reigning 'queen of the skies' was not made irrelevant overnight.

Boeing responded not with a brand-new double-decker, but by stretching its classic 747 design into the 747-8 Intercontinental. With two full passenger decks running from nose to tail, the European superjumbo dwarfed every competitor in wingspan, tail height, weight, and seating capacity. On paper, it looked as though Airbus had swept every major size and performance record in commercial flying.

However, while the Boeing jet carried fewer passengers and weighed hundreds of thousands of pounds less, it quietly held onto two major world records that the massive A380 could never take away. First, by extending the fuselage, Boeing made the 747-8 the longest airliner in service, measuring 250 feet 2 inches (76.25 meters) from nose to tail .

This made it over 11 feet longer than the A380. Second, thanks to its sharply swept wings and modern engines, the 747-8 cruises at Mach 0.855 (about 567 mph), edging out the A380’s Mach 0.85 pace to claim the title of the fastest commercial jetliner flying today.
How a Stretched Fuselage Outmaneuvered Airport Gate Limits

For one pragmatic reason, airport gates, Boeing decided to make the 747-8 longer rather than wider. Because the A380 has such an enormous wingspan, major airports had to widen taxiways and build special two-story boarding bridges just to handle it. Boeing kept the 747-8’s wingspan narrower at 224 feet 5 inches, allowing it to pull into standard international gates with minimal airport upgrades.

Boeing extended the earlier 747-400 body by 18.3 feet (5.6 meters) to create the 747-8, the longest aircraft in the sky. Two extra fuselage sections were added by engineers, one in front of and one behind the wings, increasing the overall length to 250 feet 2 inches (76.25 meters).

The 747-8 surpassed the Airbus A380 by about 11.5 feet (3.5 meters) in terms of its additional length, surpassing the previous record set by the 75.36-meter Airbus A340-600. While a four-engine Boeing remained expensive to fly, the 747-8's gate compatibility still gave airlines a practical edge over the A380.

Because the superjumbo required costly terminal upgrades and triggered higher size-based airport fees, its route map was limited to a small group of mega-hubs. By staying within standard widebody gate limits and weighing far less, the 747-8 carried over 400 passengers into a wider range of international airports with slightly lower ground costs.
1960s Wing Design & Modern Engines Deliver Boeing's Speed Crown

Boeing’s second trump card over the Airbus colossus comes down to its cruising speed world title. Rated at Mach 0.855, or roughly 567 mph at 35,000 feet, the 747-8 is the fastest commercial airliner flying today, edging out the Airbus A380, A350, and Boeing 787 at Mach 0.85, as well as the 777 at Mach 0.84.

While a speed advantage of under 1% only trims a few minutes off a long flight, it gives pilots helpful schedule padding against headwinds and arrival delays. That speed advantage comes straight from a 1960s design decision. When Boeing engineers first shaped the 747, they expected supersonic jets like Concorde to take over passenger travel.

As such, they angled the 747's wings sharply backward to help it cruise faster and keep up with high-speed air traffic. Four General Electric GEnx engines provide the power needed to take full advantage of that high-speed wing. Adapted from the Boeing 787 Dreamliner program, these modern engines produce strong thrust while burning less fuel than older 747 powerplants.

While straight wings work best at lower speeds, swept-back wings slice through high-altitude air with far less wind resistance, a shape Boeing kept on the 747-8 alongside modern, fuel-saving raked wingtips. Paired with the wing, the powerplants allow the 747-8 to cruise comfortably at Mach 0.855 without hitting the drag penalties that slow down wider, less aggressively swept airliners.
Flight-Test Setbacks & A Rocky Commercial Launch

Stretching a classic fuselage to over 250 feet in length created unexpected engineering headaches during early test flights. When pilots pushed the prototype 747-8 to high speeds, the longer body and redesigned wings experienced troublesome vibrations along the wingtips. Fixing that flexing forced Boeing to reinforce internal structures and rewrite flight-control software.

This pushed deliveries more than two years behind schedule and added over $2 billion in program costs. Once flight-test results were in, fuel economy turned out to be an even greater problem. The promised fuel-burn targets were not met by the new GEnx engines by 2.7%. That seemingly small miss wiped out the narrow cost advantage Boeing needed to convince airlines to buy a 747 instead of twinjets like the 777.

The tension exploded in September 2011, when launch customer Cargolux abruptly walked out of delivery ceremonies and refused to accept its first two jets until Boeing and General Electric offered financial discounts. Watching from the sidelines, passenger airlines grew wary of four-engine fuel and maintenance bills, choosing twinjets or the A380 instead and leaving the passenger 747-8 with very few orders.
body_zh: 卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
空中客车 A380 的推出历史性地取代了波音公司作为大型喷气式飞机制造商卫冕冠军的地位。然而，该声明有一些警告。诚然，A380 在翼展、高度、重量和载客量方面都击败了经典的波音 747，但长期统治的“天空女王”并非一夜之间变得无足轻重。
波音的回应不是推出全新的双层客机，而是将其经典的 747 设计延伸到 747-8 洲际客机中。这架欧洲巨型飞机拥有从机头到机尾的两层完整乘客甲板，在翼展、尾部高度、重量和座位容量方面令所有竞争对手相形见绌。从纸面上看，空客似乎横扫了商业飞行中所有主要尺寸和性能的记录。
然而，尽管这架波音飞机载客量减少了，重量也减轻了数十万磅，但它却悄然保持着巨大的 A380 永远无法打破的两项重要世界纪录。首先，通过延长机身，波音公司使 747-8 成为现役最长的客机，从机头到机尾长 250 英尺 2 英寸（76.25 米）。
这使得它比 A380 长超过 11 英尺。其次，凭借其后掠角大的机翼和现代化的发动机，747-8 的巡航速度为 0.855 马赫（约 567 英里/小时），超越了 A380 的 0.85 马赫速度，获得了当今飞行速度最快的商用喷气式飞机的称号。
伸展的机身如何突破机场登机口的限制
出于务实的原因，即机场登机口，波音决定将 747-8 做得更长而不是更宽。由于 A380 翼展如此巨大，各大机场不得不加宽滑行道并建造特殊的两层登机桥来应对它。波音将 747-8 的翼展保持在 224 英尺 5 英寸，使其能够以最少的机场升级进入标准国际登机口。
波音将早期的 747-400 机身延长了 18.3 英尺（5.6 米），打造出 747-8，这是天空中最长的飞机。工程师增加了两个额外的机身部分，一个在机翼前面，一个在机翼后面，将总长度增加到 250 英尺 2 英寸（76.25 米）。
就附加长度而言，747-8 比空客 A380 多出约 11.5 英尺（3.5 米），超过了此前由空客 A340-600 创下的 75.36 米纪录。虽然四引擎波音飞机的飞行成本仍然昂贵，但 747-8 的登机口兼容性仍然使航空公司比 A380 具有实际优势。
由于超级巨型飞机需要昂贵的航站楼升级，并引发更高的基于规模的机场费用，因此其航线图仅限于一小部分大型枢纽。 747-8 保持在标准宽体登机口限制范围内，且重量大大减轻，能够以略低的地面成本运载 400 多名乘客前往更广泛的国际机场。
20 世纪 60 年代的机翼设计和现代发动机成就了波音的速度之冠
波音公司相对于空中客车巨头的第二张王牌在于其巡航速度世界冠军。 747-8 的额定速度为 0.855 马赫，即在 35,000 英尺高度时的时速约为 567 英里，是当今飞行速度最快的商用客机，超过了空客 A380、A350 和波音 787（0.85 马赫）以及 777（0.84 马赫）。
虽然低于 1% 的速度优势只会使长途飞行缩短几分钟，但它可以为飞行员提供有用的时间表，以应对逆风和到达延误。这种速度优势直接来自 20 世纪 60 年代的设计决策。当波音工程师首次设计 747 时，他们期望像协和式飞机这样的超音速喷气式飞机能够接管客运出行。
因此，他们将 747 的机翼大幅向后倾斜，以帮助其更快地巡航并跟上高速空中交通。四台通用电气 GEnx 发动机提供充分利用高速机翼所需的动力。这些现代发动机改编自波音 787 梦想飞机计划，可产生强大的推力，同时比旧型 747 动力装置燃烧更少的燃料。
虽然直翼在较低速度下效果最佳，但后掠翼在高空空气中的风阻要小得多，波音公司在 747-8 上保留了这种形状以及现代、节省燃料的倾斜翼尖。与机翼配合使用的动力装置使 747-8 能够以 0.855 马赫的速度舒适地巡航，而不会受到阻力的影响，从而减慢更宽、后掠力较小的客机的速度。
飞行测试挫折和艰难的商业发布
在早期试飞期间，将经典机身拉伸至超过 250 英尺的长度造成了意想不到的工程难题。当飞行员将 747-8 原型机推向高速时，较长的机身和重新设计的机翼沿翼尖经历了麻烦的振动。解决这一问题迫使波音公司加强内部结构并重写飞行控制软件。
这使得交付时间比计划晚了两年多，并增加了超过 20 亿美元的项目成本。一旦飞行测试结果出来，燃油经济性就成为一个更大的问题。新型 GEnx 发动机未达到承诺的燃油燃烧目标 2.7%。这个看似很小的失误消除了波音说服航空公司购买 747 而不是 777 这样的双喷气机所需的狭隘成本优势。
2011 年 9 月，紧张局势爆发，当时启动客户 Cargolux 突然退出交付仪式，并拒绝接受其前两架飞机，直到波音和通用电气提供财务折扣。旁观者航空公司对四引擎燃油和维护费用越来越谨慎，转而选择双发喷气式飞机或 A380，而 747-8 客机的订单很少。

title_en: Why The Flying Wing Never Became A Commercial Airliner
title_zh: 为什么飞翼从未成为商用客机
summary: A 172-foot tailless prototype chased efficiency as early pilots wrestled with yaw instability and control limits.
summary_zh: 当早期飞行员与偏航不稳定和控制限制作斗争时，一架 172 英尺长的无尾原型机追求效率。
body_en: Airline and Airport Management Graduate, Student Commercial Pilot and Commercial Aviation Writer.

Jack Northrop envisioned a sleek, tailless future when he sent the YB-49 aloft on October 21, 1947, stretching a 172-foot (52.4 meters) wing across the desert sky without a conventional fuselage or vertical stabilizer. Promising lower drag and greater efficiency than traditional layouts, the experimental jet bomber nevertheless battled stability challenges before the second prototype crashed on June 5, 1948, killing all five crew members aboard and leading to the program winding down between 1949 and 1950.

Despite the allure of an all-wing silhouette, commercial aviation stuck with cylindrical fuselages and tailed configurations that offered predictable handling, straightforward cabin pressurization, and familiar airport compatibility. Now that digital flight controls and blended-wing concepts are bringing tailless aerodynamics back into the spotlight, what technical, operational, and commercial hurdles still stand between a flying wing concept and a viable passenger airliner?

Converted from two piston-engined YB-35 airframes, the YB-49 stretched to a 172-foot (52.4-meter) wingspan and measured 53 feet, 1 inch (16.2 meters) in length, trading propeller drives for eight Allison J35 turbojets buried inside the wing, according to The Little Aviation Museum . Removing a conventional fuselage and tail assembly allowed almost the entire planform to contribute to lift with reduced parasite drag, helping the prototype reach roughly 493 mph (793 km/h). At the same time, early turbojet fuel burn and internal volume tradeoffs tempered its range and payload flexibility relative to piston-powered designs.

Flying without a tall vertical tail meant the YB-49 had less natural stability in yaw and had delicate pitch and roll-yaw coupling, including dutch roll, during turbulent air, maneuvers, and simulated bombing runs. As noted by MiGFlug , four small vertical fins were fitted to aid directional damping, though in the late 1940s crews relied on mechanical linkages and human coordination rather than high-speed digital flight control computers to manage continuous stability corrections.

After its maiden flight on October 21, 1947, the program flew only two converted airframes before the second prototype crashed on June 5, 1948 , claiming the lives of all five crew members on board. Production orders were canceled in 1949 as Air Force leadership shifted toward competing bomber programs, and formal flight testing concluded in March 1950 before the surviving airframes were scrapped.

For an aerodynamically unstable tailless wing to become a dependable aircraft and actually work, it requires replacing purely mechanical linkages with high-speed digital fly-by-wire flight-control computers. Motion sensors can continuously measure aircraft attitude and rate changes, feeding real-time data to flight computers that command rapid, micro-adjusted deflections across trailing-edge control surfaces. That closed-loop automation damps pitch, yaw, and dutch roll oscillations far faster and more consistently than manual pilot inputs alone could achieve in earlier eras.

Digital flight control design made the Northrop B-2 Spirit possible by allowing a pure flying wing to achieve low-observable radar signatures without needing a conventional vertical tail. Instead of using a large fin that would compromise stealth, the B-2 uses computer-coordinated elevons and split drag rudders to generate controlled yawing moments and maintain crisp handling across varying weights and flight regimes. Computing redundancy and sensor voting became foundational to keeping a naturally neutral or unstable wing profile predictable from takeoff through landing.

Decades later, the Northrop B-21 Raider extends that digital control lineage into a modern low-observable bomber program built on newer avionics and computing architectures. The B-2 and B-21 demonstrate that computerized flight controls conquered the core stability and control challenges of tailless military aircraft, but solving stability in a combat airframe did not automatically translate into an airline cabin, and how to make it a reality.

The pure flying wing has not necessarily been revived, but JetZero is advancing the Z4 as a blended wing body (BWB) concept designed to carry roughly 230 to 250 passengers by smoothly merging a wide, lifting center body into outer wings. The program has gained traction through a $235 million US Air Force award supporting full-scale demonstrator development alongside plans to establish manufacturing operations in North Carolina. With a full-scale demonstrator targeted to fly in late 2027, the roadmap aims for commercial entry into service in the early 2030s if technical and regulatory hurdles are cleared on schedule.

Commercial interest in the Z4 is very real, and carriers such as Japan Airlines and United Airlines have made agreements to support the development of the aircraft . For airlines evaluating next-generation single-aisle and midsize replacements, a BWB promises lower drag and reduced fuel burn per seat compared with conventional tube-and-wing layouts. Making those conditional fleet commitments become firm deliveries, however, depends on proving that the airframe can meet strict safety, manufacturing, and operational standards at scale.

Propulsion integration sits near the center of that verification effort, including a November 2026 report from Leeham News noting that the FAA is funding a study into top-mounted engine airflow for JetZero's design. Placing engines above the aft airframe can help shield noise, but maintaining clean airflow and stable engine operation across flight conditions remains a critical engineering focus ahead of commercial certification.

A cylindrical tube naturally resists internal cabin pressure by distributing hoop stress evenly around a circular cross-section, whereas a wide, flattened wing-body hull faces far higher bending and pressure-loading demands. A non-cylindrical cabin shell tends to bow outward when pressurized at cruise altitude, so to compensate, designers need to add structural reinforcement, internal bulkheads, or load-bearing frames that add mass and complexity.

Emergency evacuation rules further add to cabin design complexity, particularly the regulatory requirement to evacuate a full aircraft within 90 seconds using half of the available exits , covered in Simple Flying analysis. Unlike a narrow single- or twin-aisle tube where passengers move linearly toward well-marked doors, a wide blended-wing cabin needs carefully engineered pathways, clear signage, and balanced exit placement, so travelers seated deep inside the layout can reach exits without bottlenecks. Cabin tiering across premium and economy zones also needs to align with aisle geometry and exit capacity rather than treating interior floor space as an open hall.
body_zh: 航空公司和机场管理毕业生、商业飞行员学生和商业航空作家。

1947 年 10 月 21 日，杰克·诺斯罗普 (Jack Northrop) 将 YB-49 送上高空，在没有传统机身或垂直安定面的情况下，将 172 英尺（52.4 米）长的机翼伸展到沙漠天空，他设想了一个光滑、无尾的未来。这款实验性喷气轰炸机承诺比传统布局具有更低的阻力和更高的效率，但在 1948 年 6 月 5 日第二架原型机坠毁之前，它一直面临着稳定性方面的挑战，导致机上五名机组人员全部遇难，并导致该项目在 1949 年至 1950 年间结束。
尽管全翼轮廓具有吸引力，但商用航空仍然采用圆柱形机身和尾翼配置，以提供可预测的操控性、简单的机舱增压和熟悉的机场兼容性。既然数字飞行控制和混合翼概念使无尾空气动力学重新成为人们关注的焦点，那么飞翼概念和可行的客机之间仍然存在哪些技术、操作和商业障碍？

据小型航空博物馆介绍，YB-49 由两个活塞发动机 YB-35 机身改装而来，翼展达到 172 英尺（52.4 米），长度为 53 英尺 1 英寸（16.2 米），用埋在机翼内的八架艾里逊 J35 涡轮喷气发动机代替螺旋桨驱动装置。去掉传统的机身和尾部组件，几乎整个平面都有助于提升升力，同时减少寄生阻力，帮助原型机达到约 493 英里/小时（793 公里/小时）的速度。与此同时，相对于活塞动力设计，早期涡轮喷气发动机的燃油燃烧和内容积权衡削弱了其航程和有效载荷的灵活性。
没有高垂直尾翼的飞行意味着 YB-49 在偏航方面的自然稳定性较差，并且在湍流空气、机动和模拟轰炸运行期间具有微妙的俯仰和滚转偏航耦合，包括荷兰滚。正如 MiGFlug 所指出的，尽管在 20 世纪 40 年代末，机组人员依靠机械联动和人类协调而不是高速数字飞行控制计算机来管理连续稳定性校正，但安装了四个小型垂直尾翼以帮助定向阻尼。
1947 年 10 月 21 日首飞后，该项目仅飞行了两架改装机身，第二架原型机于 1948 年 6 月 5 日坠毁，机上所有 5 名机组人员全部遇难。 1949 年，随着空军领导层转向竞争性轰炸机项目，生产订单被取消，正式飞行测试于 1950 年 3 月结束，随后幸存的机身被报废。
为了使空气动力学不稳定的无尾翼成为可靠的飞机并实际工作，需要用高速数字电传飞行控制计算机取代纯机械连杆。运动传感器可以连续测量飞机的姿态和速率变化，将实时数据提供给飞行计算机，从而控制后缘控制面进行快速、微调的偏转。这种闭环自动化抑制俯仰、偏航和荷兰滚振荡的速度比早期仅靠飞行员手动输入所能达到的速度和一致性要快得多。
数字飞行控制设计使诺斯罗普 B-2 精神号成为可能，它允许纯飞翼实现低可观测雷达信号，而不需要传统的垂直尾翼。 B-2 没有使用会影响隐身性的大型尾翼，而是使用计算机协调的升降副翼和分体式阻力舵来产生受控的偏航力矩，并在不同的重量和飞行状态下保持清晰的操控性。计算冗余和传感器投票成为保持自然中性或不稳定机翼轮廓从起飞到着陆可预测的基础。
几十年后，诺斯罗普 B-21 袭击者将数字控制谱系扩展到基于更新的航空电子设备和计算架构的现代低可观测轰炸机计划。 B-2 和 B-21 证明计算机化飞行控制克服了无尾军用飞机的核心稳定性和控制挑战，但解决战斗机身的稳定性并不能自动转化为机舱的稳定性，以及如何使其成为现实。

纯飞翼不一定会复兴，但 JetZero 正在将 Z4 作为混合翼体 (BWB) 概念进行推进，旨在通过将宽大的升力中心机身平稳地合并到外翼中来承载大约 230 至 250 名乘客。该计划通过美国空军拨款 2.35 亿美元支持全面验证机开发以及在北卡罗来纳州建立制造业务的计划而获得了关注。该路线图的目标是在 2027 年底进行全尺寸验证，如果技术和监管障碍如期消除，则可在 2030 年代初期投入商业使用。
Z4 的商业利益非常真实，日本航空和联合航空等航空公司已达成协议支持该飞机的开发。对于评估下一代单通道和中型飞机替代品的航空公司来说，与传统的管翼布局相比，BWB 承诺降低阻力并减少每个座位的燃油消耗。然而，让这些有条件的机队承诺成为坚定的交付，取决于证明机身能够大规模满足严格的安全、制造和运营标准。
推进集成是验证工作的核心，其中包括 Leeham News 2026 年 11 月的一篇报道，指出 FAA 正在资助一项针对 JetZero 设计的顶部安装发动机气流的研究。将发动机放置在后机身上方有助于屏蔽噪音，但在整个飞行条件下保持清洁的气流和稳定的发动机运行仍然是商业认证之前的关键工程重点。
圆柱形管通过在圆形横截面周围均匀分布环向应力来自然地抵抗内部机舱压力，而宽而扁平的翼体船体则面临更高的弯曲和压力负载要求。非圆柱形机舱外壳在巡航高度受压时往往会向外弯曲，因此为了补偿，设计人员需要添加结构加固、内部舱壁或承载框架，从而增加质量和复杂性。
紧急疏散规则进一步增加了机舱设计的复杂性，特别是简单飞行分析中涉及的在 90 秒内使用一半可用出口疏散整架飞机的监管要求。与狭窄的单通道或双通道通道不同，乘客直线走向标记清晰的舱门，宽阔的混合翼客舱需要精心设计的通道、清晰的标志和平衡的出口位置，以便坐在布局深处的旅客可以无障碍地到达出口。高级区和经济区的客舱分层还需要与过道几何形状和出口容量保持一致，而不是将内部地板空间视为开放式大厅。

title_en: Private Pilot Disputes Trump’s Claim That He Used Non-US ATC To Fly In US Airspace Before Office
title_zh: 私人飞行员对特朗普关于他在上任前使用非美国空中交通管制在美国领空飞行的说法提出异议
summary: A private pilot challenges Trump's renewed claims about foreign air traffic control as the FAA faces renewed scrutiny.
summary_zh: 随着美国联邦航空局面临新的审查，一名私人飞行员对特朗普关于外国空中交通管制的新主张提出质疑。
body_en: Paul has had a career of 25+ years focused on the international technology sector, which has taken him to over 100 countries. Along the way, he developed a deep love for aviation, with a travel bucket list measured by aircraft types flown rather than destinations reached. Now he brings that avgeek passion, along with the journalism experience he accumulated early in his career, to write insightful pieces for Simple Flying.

President Trump has revived a claim that his private pilot previously relied on another country's air traffic control (ATC) system while flying in the US, prompting a public rebuttal from a private pilot. Speaking during a White House press conference on Friday, Trump criticized America's aviation infrastructure while discussing recent disruptions affecting the country's airspace, according to National Public Radio (NPR) .

The comments came one week after a nationwide FAA ground stop disrupted thousands of flights and just days after the administration requested another $50.1 billion for aviation modernization. However, Trump's account of using foreign controllers has raised questions about whether he meant air traffic control or the navigation technology installed aboard his aircraft.
Private Pilot Challenges Trump's Air Traffic Control Claim

According to the Daily Beast , Trump made the remarks during a "bonkers appearance" at a White House press conference addressing recent disruptions involving aviation, banking and communications networks. Asked about the incidents, the president maintained that they were unrelated, before discussing his personal experiences with private aviation.
Trump described US ATC infrastructure as "ancient" , and said that his pilot had used foreign air traffic control before he entered office.

“It's ancient! In fact, you know, before I was here, I had a plane. I had a very nice life. And my pilot would use the air traffic control from a totally different country. This was years ago, before I was in office. I don't want to say the country, but he found one country better than ours.”

The assertion prompted a response from journalist Brian Karem, who identified himself as a private pilot. In a post on X , Karem disputed the suggestion that pilots operating in US airspace could bypass domestic controllers by seeking assistance from another country. His objection centered on the distinction between the authorities controlling airspace and the equipment pilots use to navigate.
"You cannot call up ATC in Europe and say, 'Hey give me a hand. I'm flying over US airspace.'"

Trump's remarks were not entirely new. During the National Prayer Breakfast in February last year, he similarly claimed to use equipment or services from another country when landing his private aircraft in New York, according to Anadolu Ajansı . The comments attracted scrutiny from aviation experts at the time, Forbes reported.
Trump Appears To Confuse Air Traffic Control With Aircraft Navigation Systems

President Trump likely confused air traffic control systems with onboard navigation technology, according to Forbes. Retired airline pilot and aviation safety expert John Cox explained that pilots operating under ATC supervision must comply with the applicable rules of that country, regardless of their navigation equipment's country of origin.

Air traffic control and aircraft navigation perform very different functions. Controllers issue clearances, instructions and traffic information, while onboard navigation systems help pilots determine their position and follow flight plans. An aircraft operating under instrument flight rules in controlled US airspace cannot simply select a foreign ATC provider. The differences are summarized below
Provides clearances, traffic separation and instructions
Provides satellite-based positioning and navigation
Calculates and manages the aircraft's flight path
Tracks aircraft position and movement using onboard sensors
Provide route, waypoint and procedure information
Provide navigation, communication or flight management capabilities

A plausible explanation is that Trump's aircraft used internationally manufactured avionics, navigation databases, or satellite-based positioning technology. As the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) Aeronautical Information Manual explains, these technologies provide navigation guidance but do not replace ATC services. Without confirmation from Trump's former pilots, the precise technology he was describing remains unknown.
body_zh: Paul 拥有超过 25 年的职业生涯，专注于国际技术领域，足迹遍及 100 多个国家。一路走来，他对航空产生了深深的热爱，他的旅行愿望清单是根据飞行的飞机类型而不是到达的目的地来衡量的。现在，他带着这种平均极客的热情，以及他在职业生涯早期积累的新闻经验，为《简单飞行》撰写了富有洞察力的文章。
特朗普总统再次声称，他的私人飞行员此前在美国飞行时依赖另一个国家的空中交通管制（ATC）系统，此举引发了一名私人飞行员的公开反驳。据美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 报道，特朗普在周五的白宫新闻发布会上发表讲话时，批评了美国的航空基础设施，同时讨论了最近影响该国领空的干扰事件。
这一评论是在美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 全国范围内的一次地面停留导致数千架航班中断一周后发表的，而就在几天前，政府还要求再拨款 501 亿美元用于航空现代化。然而，特朗普关于使用外国管制员的说法引发了人们的质疑：他指的是空中交通管制还是飞机上安装的导航技术。
私人飞行员挑战特朗普的空中交通管制主张
据《每日野兽报》报道，特朗普在白宫新闻发布会上“疯狂亮相”，讨论了最近涉及航空、银行和通信网络的干扰问题。当被问及这些事​​件时，总统坚称这些事件无关，然后讨论了他在私人航空方面的个人经历。
特朗普称美国空中交通管制基础设施“古老”，并表示他的飞行员在就职前曾使用过外国空中交通管制。
“它很古老！事实上，你知道，在我来这里之前，我有一架飞机。我过着非常美好的生活。我的飞行员会使用来自完全不同国家的空中交通管制。那是几年前，在我上任之前。我不想说那个国家，但他发现有一个国家比我们的更好。”
这一说法引起了记者布莱恩·卡雷姆的回应，他自称是一名私人飞行员。在 X 上的一篇帖子中，卡雷姆对在美国领空飞行的飞行员可以通过寻求其他国家的援助来绕过国内管制员的建议提出了异议。他的反对意见集中在控制空域的当局与飞行员用于导航的设备之间的区别。
“你不能打电话给欧洲的空中交通管制并说，‘嘿，帮我一下。我正在美国领空飞行。’”
特朗普的言论并不新鲜。据阿纳多卢·阿詹西 (Anadolu Ajansı) 报道，在去年 2 月的全国祈祷早餐会上，他同样声称在他的私人飞机降落在纽约时使用了来自另一个国家的设备或服务。据《福布斯》报道，这些言论引起了当时航空专家的密切关注。
特朗普似乎将空中交通管制与飞机导航系统混为一谈
据《福布斯》报道，特朗普总统可能将空中交通管制系统与机载导航技术混淆了。退休航空公司飞行员和航空安全专家约翰·考克斯解释说，在空中交通管制监督下操作的飞行员必须遵守该国的适用规则，无论其导航设备的原产国如何。
空中交通管制和飞机导航执行截然不同的功能。管制员发布许可、指令和交通信息，而机载导航系统则帮助飞行员确定其位置并遵循飞行计划。在美国受控空域内按照仪表飞行规则运行的飞机不能简单地选择外国空中交通管制提供商。差异总结如下
提供许可、交通隔离和指示
提供卫星定位和导航
计算和管理飞机的飞行路径
使用机载传感器跟踪飞机位置和运动
提供路线、航点和程序信息
提供导航、通信或飞行管理功能
一个合理的解释是，特朗普的飞机使用了国际制造的航空电子设备、导航数据库或卫星定位技术。正如美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 航空信息手册所解释的那样，这些技术提供导航指导，但不会取代 ATC 服务。未经特朗普前飞行员的证实，他所描述的确切技术仍然未知。

title_en: Flexibility: How Flight Attendants Can Be Displaced From Their Schedule With Little Notice
title_zh: 灵活性：如何在几乎没有通知的情况下将空乘人员从他们的日程安排中取代
summary: Rarely does a schedule go to plan.
summary_zh: 日程表很少能按计划进行。
body_en: Writer - Patricia joins Simple Flying with over 20 years of experience in aviation. She has served as cabin crew on flights from economy-class through to first-class and on private jets as well as being head of cabin crew and cabin safety focal point. Patricia has a master's level postgraduate diploma in Human Factors in Aviation and has written about aviation since 2010. Based in Dubai/Cyprus.

Flight attendants ' schedules in the US can change at short notice in several ways, but union contracts set limits on how it happens and what they're paid when it does. This guide will take a closer look at how it all works, when things change at the last minute, and what can happen to a flight attendant's schedule.

In the rest of the world, it's a little bit different, and unions rarely have much input. It's all down to the airlines' operations teams and aviation regulators when it comes to how our schedules can change. Of course, flexibility is key, and things can happen unexpectedly, but that's all part of the fun of being a flight attendant or cabin crew .

When a trip or part of a trip is canceled, crew scheduling can move the affected flight attendant to another trip, put them on reserve/standby, or release them from duty entirely. One older contract, filed with the SEC , pays them for whichever is greater: the original assignment or the new one. Many US airline contracts call this "pay protection." This is a contractual rule that keeps a flight attendant's scheduled pay credit safe when flights change, get canceled, or get delayed through no fault of their own.

If the trip or a leg of the sequence is canceled, union collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) typically guarantee that they still get paid for the original scheduled value or the new assigned trip, whichever is greater. If crew scheduling alters the route or equipment after a disruption, pay protection ensures that they do not lose money if the new assignment ends up paying less than what was originally on the line.

Alaska Airlines' current agreement , for example, can remove a flight attendant from an assignment with pay protection and fly them home as a passenger; this is called deadheading. Under the 2025-2028 Collective Bargaining Agreement between Alaska Airlines and the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, line-holding flight attendants receive 150% pay on top of strong base trip protection when crew scheduling reassigns or reroutes a sequence. If a crew member is assigned to four or more legs over the original sequence, pay is 200%.

Trip displacement occurs when a crew member is involuntarily removed from a scheduled flight pairing or stranded away from their planned itinerary. This could be due to operational needs, regulatory limits, or personnel bumps; it is not a personal absence from duty. It can vary from airline to airline in the US, and union contracts may vary. At carriers without union contracts, such as Delta Air Lines, displaced flight attendants often do not receive automatic pay protection and must choose between sitting on-call availability or taking a lesser payment.

A flight attendant can also be bumped from a trip that they bid for. They can be displaced from trips to make room for training or for new hires' supervised flights, which are called operating experience. A flight attendant can be pulled from a trip so a supervisor, for example, can occupy that position for qualification or observation. In those cases, the displaced flight attendant gets a similar trip or is released from duty for the rest of the trip.

Frontier Airlines' 2019 contract requires at least 24 hours' notice before a flight attendant is displaced, and pays them for the trip they lost. Depending on the contract, crew scheduling may have a specific window (often matching the original trip's footprint) to assign replacement flights. If the airline does not reassign the flight attendant within those rules, the crew member is released with pay.

The one thing that most often catches US flight attendants off guard is the junior assignment, sometimes called junior availability or JA. This is a last-resort scheduling measure where an airline forces the most junior legal flight attendant to work a flight during their scheduled day off or open time because all reserve crews have been exhausted . This prevents cancellations or other disruptions when the reserve pool runs out, and it typically falls on the most junior available flight attendant.

This is used in cases such as major weather disruptions, holiday travel spikes, or high sick-call volume, after all on-call reserve flight attendants have already been assigned. Airlines assign these open trips starting from the absolute bottom of the seniority list at that base and working upward until the flight is covered. However, the new trip cannot violate mandatory rest requirements or maximum duty limits. This will also attract a premium payment, and the airline has to restore any lost days off.

Contracts usually limit how often junior assignments can happen. PSA Airlines' contract caps it at three days a month and bars assignments that are more than 24 hours in advance, while Silver Airways' contract limits it to twice a month. They also usually pay at a premium rate of 150% at Silver Airways and PSA Airlines, and 2.5 times the trip rate under Alaska Airlines' 2025–2028 contract. Silver Airways closed down in June 2025.

At some airlines , flight attendants who are already on duty at the airport, such as those arriving, checking in, or waiting in between flights, can be drafted onto another flight when time is critical, or the reserve pool is empty. Therefore, their entire schedule can change if a new trip is added or removed. Usually, crew scheduling tries not to disrupt the schedule too much and swaps them with a trip with similar timing, but of course, this is not always possible.

Flight attendants on reserve or standby are usually more junior crew with low seniority, are on call, and can be given trips with little notice. Many US-based crew start out on reserve and may do so for the first few years. At American Airlines, for example, flight attendants are on reserve for the first year and then move to one month on reserve, one month off reserve until year five, when it moves to one month on reserve and three months off according to their APFA contract .

At Delta Air Lines , junior flight attendants bid on a line and do not have to complete a full month on reserve. Instead, they have six 'A' days a month, where they are on call. If a Delta flight attendant's trip is canceled or removed, they only keep their pay if they convert to availability. Delta's order of assignment places displaced lineholders on availability ahead of A-Day reserves, and management holds broader discretion to modify trips during irregular operations.
body_zh: 作家 - Patricia 加入 Simple Flying 时拥有 20 多年的航空经验。她曾在从经济舱到头等舱的航班以及私人飞机上担任机组人员，并担任机组人员负责人和客舱安全协调员。 Patricia 拥有航空人为因素硕士学位研究生文凭，自 2010 年以来一直撰写有关航空的文章。居住在迪拜/塞浦路斯。
在美国，空乘人员的日程安排可能会在短时间内以多种方式发生变化，但工会合同对这种变化的发生方式以及变化时的报酬设定了限制。本指南将仔细研究这一切是如何运作的，当事情在最后一刻发生变化时，以及空乘人员的日程安排会发生什么变化。
在世界其他地方，情况略有不同，工会很少有太多投入。当谈到我们的航班时刻表如何改变时，这完全取决于航空公司的运营团队和航空监管机构。当然，灵活性是关键，事情可能会发生意外，但这就是作为空乘人员或机组人员的乐趣的一部分。
当一次旅行或部分旅行被取消时，机组人员可以将受影响的空乘人员转移到另一次旅行，将他们置于保留/待命状态，或者完全让他们停止执勤。向美国证券交易委员会提交的一份较旧的合同向他们支付较高的费用：原始转让或新转让。许多美国航空公司的合同将其称为“薪酬保护”。这是一项合同规则，可在航班变更、取消或非因空乘人员自身过错而延误时确保空乘人员的预定工资信用安全。
如果行程或行程中的某一段被取消，工会集体谈判协议 (CBA) 通常会保证他们仍能获得原计划价值或新指定行程的报酬，以较高者为准。如果机组人员调度在中断后改变路线或设备，工资保护可确保他们在新任务最终支付的费用低于线路上原来的费用时不会损失金钱。
例如，阿拉斯加航空公司目前的协议可以取消空乘人员的工作并提供工资保障，并将他们作为乘客带回家；这称为死头。根据阿拉斯加航空与空乘人员协会 (CWA) 之间的 2025-2028 年集体谈判协议，当机组人员安排重新分配或重新安排序列时，在强大的基本旅行保护之外，排队空乘人员还可获得 150% 的工资。如果一名机组人员被分配到原始序列的 4 个或更多航段，则工资为 200%。
当机组成员非自愿地从预定的航班配对中移除或被困在计划行程之外时，就会发生行程流离失所。这可能是由于运营需求、监管限制或人员变动所致；这不是个人旷工。美国各航空公司的规定可能有所不同，工会合同也可能有所不同。在达美航空等没有工会合同的航空公司，被解雇的空乘人员通常无法获得自动工资保障，必须在随叫随到或收取较少的工资之间做出选择。
空乘人员也可能会被赶出他们竞标的行程。他们可能会因出差而被取代，以便为培训或新员工的监督飞行腾出空间，这被称为操作经验。空乘人员可以从旅行中被召回，这样主管就可以占据该职位进行资格认证或观察。在这些情况下，被取代的空乘人员将获得类似的旅行，或者在剩余的旅行中被免职。
边疆航空 2019 年的合同要求空乘人员在离开之前至少提前 24 小时发出通知，并向他们支付损失的行程费用。根据合同，机组人员安排可能有一个特定的窗口（通常与原始行程的足迹相匹配）来分配替代航班。如果航空公司不按照这些规则重新分配空乘人员，则该机组人员将被带薪解雇。
最常让美国空乘人员措手不及的一件事是初级任务，有时称为初级可用性或 JA。这是最后的调度措施，航空公司强迫最低级别的合法空乘人员在预定的休息日或开放时间工作，因为所有后备机组人员都已经精疲力尽。当储备池用完时，这可以防止取消或其他中断，并且通常由资历最浅的空乘人员负责。
这适用于重大天气干扰、假日旅行高峰或病假电话量大等情况，而所有待命的后备空乘人员已经被分配完毕。航空公司从该基地资历列表的绝对底部开始分配这些开放旅行，然后向上分配，直到航班被覆盖。但是，新的行程不能违反强制性休息要求或最高职责限制。这也将吸引额外费用，并且航空公司必须恢复任何损失的休息日。
合同通常会限制初级任务的发生频率。 PSA 航空公司的合同限制为每月 3 天，并且禁止提前 24 小时以上进行任务，而 Silver Airways 的合同则限制为每月两次。他们通常还支付 Silver Airways 和 PSA Airlines 150% 的溢价，以及阿拉斯加航空 2025-2028 年合同中行程费率的 2.5 倍。银色航空于 2025 年 6 月关闭。
在某些航空公司，当时间紧迫或储备库已空时，可以将已经在机场值班的空乘人员（例如抵达、办理登机手续或在航班之间等待的空乘人员）安排到另一航班。因此，如果添加或删除新的行程，他们的整个日程可能会发生变化。通常，机组人员的日程安排会尽量不要过多地打乱时间表，而是将其与时间相似的行程进行交换，但当然，这并不总是可能的。
预备或待命的空乘人员通常是资历较低的初级机组人员，随时待命，并且可以在很少通知的情况下进行旅行。许多美国船员一开始都是预备役，并且可能会在最初几年这样做。例如，在美国航空，空乘人员第一年处于预备役状态，然后变为一个月预备役，一个月休息，直到第五年，根据 APFA 合同，第五年变为一个月预备役，三个月休息。
在达美航空，初级空乘人员可以在航线上竞标，并且不必完成一整月的预订。相反，他们每个月有六天“A”日待命。如果达美航空乘务员的行程被取消或取消，他们只有在转为可用的情况下才能保留工资。达美航空的分配顺序将流离失所的线路乘客安排在全日储备之前，并且管理层拥有更广泛的自由裁量权，可以在不定期运营期间修改行程。

title_en: Third Time’s Not The Charm: A SWISS A220’s Odd Triple Aborted Takeoff
title_zh: 第三次没有魅力：瑞士航空 A220 奇怪的三次起飞失败
summary: A SWISS Airbus A220 rejected its takeoff from Zurich three times in a row before returning to the gate. The cause was a stuck auto-thrust switch.
summary_zh: 一架瑞航空客 A220 从苏黎世起飞，连续三次拒绝起飞，然后才返回登机口。原因是自动推力开关卡住。
body_en: If you’re a frequent flyer, odds are that you’ve encountered an aborted takeoff, whereby the plane accelerates down the runway, only to slow down, and eventually come to a stop. In some cases this can feel like a non-event, while in other cases it can feel much scarier, depending on the speed at which the takeoff is aborted.

However, here’s something you don’t often see — a SWISS Airbus A220 aborted its takeoff three times in a row, before finally returning to the gate to see what was going on, as reported by Blick . The explanation is actually quite logical, but that doesn’t make the whole ordeal any less unusual.
SWISS Airbus A220 aborted Zurich takeoff three times

On Tuesday, November 17, 2026, SWISS flight LX2110 was scheduled to operate from Zurich (ZRH) to Malaga (AGP), with a 9:35AM departure. The flight was operated by an Airbus A220-300 with the registration code HB-JCM.

The plane pushed back and taxied out to the runway right on schedule. The pilots began the takeoff roll, but then quickly applied the brakes, causing the plane to come to a stop, while still at a slow speed. The pilots took a moment to run checklists, and then decided on another takeoff attempt, only for the same thing to happen again!

After the second aborted takeoff, the captain reportedly informed passengers that the thrust levers had popped out during the takeoff roll, and that was the reason for the aborted takeoff. However, rather than returning to the gate, they decided to attempt an additional takeoff roll.

Once again, the takeoff was aborted. At that point the captain explained that nothing like this had ever happened to him before in his 12 year career, and that the plane would be returning to the gate.

There ended up being a plane change, and then the A220 with the registration code HB-JCO was assigned to operate this flight — it ended up taking off at 1:29PM and landing at 3:52PM, around 3.5 hours behind schedule.
So, what explains this trio of aborted takeoffs?
A SWISS spokesperson confirmed the incident happened, though noted that the takeoffs were aborted at a low speed of around 50 kilometers per hour (around 30 miles per hour).

What explains the aborted takeoffs? Well, it was because as the plane accelerated for takeoff, the automatic thrust control system automatically deactivated. To explain this as simply as possible, as I understand it, on the A220 when the auto-thrust is armed and the thrust levers are moved forward for takeoff, the auto-thrust then takes over, and moves the levers forward without manual intervention.

In other words, one of the pilots keeps their hands on the auto-thrust levers and “moves” with them, but doesn’t actually apply any force. Pilots are trained this way, and to not manually apply force. In the event that the crew tries to stop the auto-thrust lever motion, a pressure switch detects this, and then disengages the auto-thrust, to allow for a manual override.

In this case, the auto-thrust incorrectly detected resistance, when the pilots weren’t attempting to apply it. According to the airline, the system that monitors the aircraft’s technical status in real time was unable to identify the cause of the error, as no errors were displayed in the system. So at first, the pilots likely wondered if they had accidentally applied force.

However, once technicians had a look at the plane, it was discovered that the switch for disabling the automatic thrust control on the original aircraft was stuck, and this caused the automatic thrust control to shut down during takeoff attempts.

So while this can understandably seem scary to passengers, this wasn’t even a direct safety issue. After all, the pilots could’ve also manually moved the throttles. However, you also don’t want to take off when you know there’s an issue with the throttles, since that’s not exactly a best practice.
A SWISS Airbus A220 attempted a takeoff from Zurich three times in a row. While I’ve had two consecutive aborted takeoffs, I’ve never had three, and I can’t imagine that happens all too often.

While this is unusual, it sounds like this was handled well, and I can see why the pilots kept trying. This wasn’t a critical safety issue, but instead, just an incorrect detection of inputs, in a way that wouldn’t really pose a risk to the flight. At the same time, you don’t want to knowingly take off with a fault switch.
What do you make of this SWISS aborted takeoff trio?
body_zh: 如果您经常乘坐飞机，您很可能遇到过起飞中止的情况，飞机在跑道上加速，然后减速，最终停下来。在某些情况下，这可能感觉像是一件小事，而在其他情况下，它可能感觉更可怕，具体取决于起飞中止的速度。
然而，据 Blick 报道，有一种情况并不常见——一架瑞航空客 A220 飞机连续三次中止起飞，最后才返回登机口查看发生了什么事。这个解释实际上很合乎逻辑，但这并没有让整个考验变得不那么不寻常。
瑞航空客A220苏黎世起飞三次中止
2026 年 11 月 17 日星期二，瑞航 LX2110 航班原定从苏黎世 (ZRH) 飞往马拉加 (AGP)，起飞时间为上午 9:35。该航班由空客 A220-300 运营，注册代码为 HB-JCM。
飞机按计划后退并滑行至跑道。飞行员开始起飞滑跑，但随后迅速踩下刹车，导致飞机停了下来，但速度仍然很慢。飞行员花了一些时间检查清单，然后决定再次尝试起飞，结果同样的事情再次发生！
据报道，在第二次起飞中止后，机长告诉乘客，推力杆在起飞滑跑过程中弹出，这就是起飞中止的原因。然而，他们没有返回登机口，而是决定尝试额外的起飞滑跑。
起飞再次中止。此时，机长解释说，在他 12 年的职业生涯中，他从未发生过这样的事情，飞机将返回登机口。
最终更换了飞机，然后分配了注册代码为 HB-JCO 的 A220 来运营该航班 - 最终于下午 1:29 起飞，下午 3:52 降落，比原计划晚了约 3.5 小时。
那么，如何解释这三次起飞失败呢？
瑞士航空发言人证实了这起事件的发生，但指出起飞在大约每小时 50 公里（大约每小时 30 英里）的低速下中止。
如何解释起飞中止？嗯，这是因为当飞机加速起飞时，自动推力控制系统自动停用。为了尽可能简单地解释这一点，据我了解，在 A220 上，当自动推力启动并且推力杆向前移动以起飞时，自动推力然后接管，并将推力杆向前移动，无需手动干预。
换句话说，其中一名飞行员将手放在自动推力杆上并随之“移动”，但实际上并没有施加任何力。飞行员接受这样的训练，并且不会手动施加力量。如果机组人员试图停止自动推力杆运动，压力开关会检测到这一情况，然后断开自动推力杆，以允许手动超控。
在这种情况下，当飞行员没有尝试应用自动推力时，自动推力错误地检测到了阻力。据该航空公司称，实时监控飞机技术状态的系统无法识别错误原因，因为系统中没有显示任何错误。因此，一开始，飞行员可能想知道他们是否不小心用力了。
然而，技术人员检查飞机后发现，原机上禁用自动推力控制的开关被卡住，导致自动推力控制在起飞时关闭。
因此，虽然这对乘客来说似乎很可怕，这是可以理解的，但这甚至不是直接的安全问题。毕竟，飞行员也可以手动移动油门。然而，当您知道油门出现问题时，您也不想起飞，因为这并不是最佳实践。
一架瑞士空客 A220 连续三次尝试从苏黎世起飞。虽然我连续两次中止起飞，但从未有过三次，而且我无法想象这种情况会经常发生。
虽然这很不寻常，但听起来处理得很好，我可以理解飞行员为什么不断尝试。这并不是一个严重的安全问题，而只是输入检测不正确，不会对飞行造成真正的风险。同时，您也不想故意带着故障开关起飞。
您如何看待瑞航这起中止起飞的三人组？

title_en: 2 Virgin Australia Pilots Admit They’re Too Tired To Continue Flying, Immediately Offloaded
title_zh: 维珍澳大利亚航空 2 名飞行员承认太累，无法继续飞行，立即卸货
summary: Two Australian pilots reported fatigue aboard a Boeing 737 flight to Adelaide and were immediately stood down, highlighting aviation safety protocols
summary_zh: 两名澳大利亚飞行员报告在飞往阿德莱德的波音 737 航班上感到疲劳，并立即被停职，强调了航空安全协议
body_en: Experienced ICAO English Language Proficiency Instructor for pilots and ATCOs and conference interpreter who is passionate about facilitating effective communication within aviation-related businesses. Possess a deep understanding of the aviation industry, including aviation regulations, terminology, and industry-specific communication protocols. Has been working at numerous airshows across Europe since 2014. Being an ultralight pilot in her free time, she also promotes safety and efficiency in aviation operations.

Two Virgin Australia pilots declared themselves unfit to continue flying after fatigue set in during a domestic flight from Melbourne Airport (MEL) to Adelaide Airport (ADL ) on Wednesday. Both crew members requested to be stood down upon reaching their destination. The aircraft landed safely at Adelaide Airport, after which the pilots were immediately removed from further flying duties.

The incident highlights the importance of fatigue management in commercial aviation, where pilots must recognize when tiredness could compromise their ability to operate an aircraft safely. Although the flight itself was completed without incident, the decision to remove both pilots raises broader questions about crew scheduling, rest periods, and the challenges of managing fatigue across Australia's airline industry. Virgin Australia's response also shows why self-reporting remains essential to aviation safety.
Both Pilots Reported Fatigue During Flight VA219

According to AIRLIVE , the incident occurred aboard VA219 on Wednesday morning. The Boeing 737-800, registered VH-VUX, was operating a domestic service between Melbourne and Adelaide when both pilots reported fatigue. Rather than continue their planned duties, the flight crew requested to be stood down at their next destination.

The aircraft continued to Adelaide and completed its journey safely, touching down at 11:05 local time. The flight had departed Melbourne about an hour earlier, following the aircraft's previous operation of flight VA814 from Sydney to Melbourne earlier that morning. Once in Adelaide, both pilots were immediately offloaded, preventing them from operating any subsequent flight sectors until they were considered fit to return to duty.

The decision followed Virgin Australia's fatigue risk management procedures, which allow pilots to report when tiredness affects their ability to perform their responsibilities safely. Importantly, declaring oneself unfit to fly is not an admission of wrongdoing. It is a safety measure designed to prevent potentially impaired crew members from continuing operations.
Fatigue Has Previously Raised Concerns In Australia

This is not the first time fatigue management has attracted attention at Virgin Australia. In May 2024, The Guardian reported that senior pilots had raised concerns about the airline's rostering arrangements, arguing that demanding schedules were contributing to fatigue across the pilot workforce. Correspondence reviewed by the newspaper highlighted concerns about consecutive long duty days, sometimes lasting 11–12 hours, followed by the minimum 12-hour rest period permitted under the applicable rules.

The pilots also questioned the airline's rostering software and its ability to accommodate operational realities, particularly when flights were delayed. Virgin Australia responded at the time by saying it operated under a robust fatigue management system approved by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA). The airline also highlighted that its pilots received 156 rostered days off annually. Although those earlier concerns do not establish the cause of the November 2026 report, they illustrate how crew scheduling and fatigue have remained important topics within the airline.

Fatigue is also a concern beyond the flight deck. Last month, ABC News reported on an Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) investigation into a taxiway incident at Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport (SYD ) involving Virgin Australia flight 1589 and Qantas flight 420. An air traffic controller working during the incident had a high predicted fatigue risk after being rostered to finish at 8:50 PM and return to duty at 5:30 AM the following morning. The ATSB stressed that a high predicted fatigue level does not necessarily mean an individual is actually fatigued. Nevertheless, the case demonstrates how demanding schedules can affect safety-critical aviation personnel across different operational environments.
Why Removing Fatigued Pilots Is The Right Decision

Fatigue can significantly affect a pilot's concentration, reaction time, memory, and decision-making under pressure. According to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), tiredness can reduce the ability to perform tasks requiring manual coordination, vigilance, and higher-level cognitive processing. These effects can develop after a single demanding period or accumulate over several days of insufficient rest.

The consequences can be particularly serious in commercial aviation, where pilots must continuously monitor aircraft systems, communicate with air traffic control, assess changing weather conditions, and respond to unexpected situations. Even experienced flight crew members are not immune to these effects. The FAA also notes that coffee, medication, motivation, and willpower cannot overcome fatigue; adequate sleep remains the most effective solution .

Virgin Australia's decision to remove both pilots from further duties should be viewed positively. Allowing fatigued crew members to keep flying just to avoid disruption would create an unnecessary safety risk for passengers, other crew members, and everyone involved in the operation. While replacing pilots can create scheduling complications and potentially delay subsequent services, those considerations must remain secondary to operational safety.

This incident demonstrates an important principle of commercial aviation: a flight is only safe when its crew members are fit to perform their duties. By allowing both pilots to report their condition and immediately standing them down after arrival, Virgin Australia followed the appropriate safety-first approach.
body_zh: 经验丰富的国际民航组织飞行员和空中交通管制员英语语言能力讲师以及会议口译员，热衷于促进航空相关业务中的有效沟通。对航空业有深入的了解，包括航空法规、术语和行业特定的通信协议。自 2014 年以来，她一直在欧洲各地的众多航展上工作。作为一名超轻型飞行员，她在业余时间还致力于提高航空运营的安全性和效率。
周三，维珍澳大利亚航空的两名飞行员在从墨尔本机场 (MEL) 飞往阿德莱德机场 (ADL) 的国内航班上感到疲劳后，宣布不适合继续飞行。两名机组人员在到达目的地后都要求停下来。飞机安全降落在阿德莱德机场，随后飞行员立即不再执行进一步的飞行任务。
该事件凸显了疲劳管理在商业航空中的重要性，飞行员必须认识到疲劳何时会损害他们安全操作飞机的能力。尽管飞行本身没有发生任何事故，但解雇两名飞行员的决定引发了有关机组人员安排、休息时间以及澳大利亚航空业疲劳管理挑战的更广泛问题。维珍澳大利亚航空的回应也表明了为什么自我报告对于航空安全仍然至关重要。
两名飞行员均报告在 VA219 航班中感到疲劳
据 AIRLIVE 报道，该事件发生在周三上午的 VA219 航班上。这架注册号为 VH-VUX 的波音 737-800 正在墨尔本和阿德莱德之间运营国内航班，两名飞行员均报告疲劳。机组人员没有继续执行计划中的任务，而是要求在下一个目的地停留。
飞机继续飞往阿德莱德，并安全完成旅程，于当地时间11时05分落地。该航班于当天早上早些时候执飞从悉尼飞往墨尔本的 VA814 航班，大约提前一小时从墨尔本起飞。抵达阿德莱德后，两名飞行员立即被遣散，禁止他们执行任何后续航段，直到他们被认为适合重返岗位。
该决定遵循维珍澳大利亚航空的疲劳风险管理程序，该程序允许飞行员在疲劳影响其安全履行职责的能力时进行报告。重要的是，声明自己不适合飞行并不意味着承认有不当行为。这是一项安全措施，旨在防止可能受损的机组人员继续作业。
疲劳此前曾在澳大利亚引起担忧
这并不是疲劳管理第一次引起维珍澳大利亚航空的关注。 2024 年 5 月，《卫报》报道称，高级飞行员对该航空公司的排班安排表示担忧，认为严格的时间表导致飞行员队伍疲劳。该报查阅的信件强调了对连续长时间工作的担忧，有时持续 11 至 12 小时，然后是适用规则允许的至少 12 小时休息时间。
飞行员还质疑该航空公司的排班软件及其适应运营现实的能力，特别是在航班延误时。维珍澳大利亚航空当时回应称，该公司在民航安全局（CASA）批准的强大疲劳管理系统下运营。该航空公司还强调，其飞行员每年享受 156 个轮休日。尽管这些早期的担忧并未确定 2026 年 11 月报告的原因，但它们说明了机组人员调度和疲劳仍然是航空公司内部的重要话题。

疲劳也是驾驶舱以外的一个问题。上个月，美国广播公司新闻报道了澳大利亚运输安全局 (ATSB) 对悉尼金斯福德·史密斯机场 (SYD) 涉及维珍澳大利亚航空 1589 号航班和澳洲航空 420 号航班的滑行道事故进行的调查。事故期间工作的一名空中交通管制员被安排在晚上 8:50 结束工作并于第二天早上 5:30 返回工作岗位，预计疲劳风险很高。 ATSB 强调，预测的疲劳程度较高并不一定意味着个人实际上已经疲劳。尽管如此，该案例表明，严格的时间表会对不同运营环境中的安全关键航空人员产生怎样的影响。
为什么解雇疲劳的飞行员是正确的决定
疲劳会严重影响飞行员在压力下的注意力、反应时间、记忆力和决策能力。根据美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 的说法，疲劳会降低执行需要手动协调、警惕性和高级认知处理的任务的能力。这些影响可能会在一次高强度时期后出现，或者在几天休息不足后累积。
在商业航空中，后果可能尤其严重，飞行员必须持续监控飞机系统、与空中交通管制部门沟通、评估不断变化的天气条件并对意外情况做出反应。即使是经验丰富的机组人员也不能幸免于这些影响。美国联邦航空局还指出，咖啡、药物、动力和意志力无法克服疲劳；充足的睡眠仍然是最有效的解决办法。
维珍澳大利亚航空解除两名飞行员进一步职务的决定应该得到积极看待。允许疲惫的机组人员继续飞行以避免干扰，会给乘客、其他机组人员以及参与操作的每个人带来不必要的安全风险。虽然更换飞行员可能会造成调度复杂化并可能延迟后续服务，但这些考虑因素必须放在运营安全的次要位置。
这一事件体现了商业航空的一个重要原则：只有机组人员能够正常履行职责，航班才是安全的。维珍澳大利亚航空允许两名飞行员报告他们的状况并在他们抵达后立即让他们停飞，从而遵循了适当的安全第一的方法。

title_en: Avelo Airlines Makes Tiny US Airport Its New No. 2: Here's Why
title_zh: 阿维洛航空公司 (Avelo Airlines) 将美国小型机场打造成新的第二大机场：原因如下
summary: From Florida to Las Vegas Avelo rolls out multiple daily and weekly services that reshape North Texas travel options.
summary_zh: 从佛罗里达州到拉斯维加斯，Avelo 推出了多项每日和每周服务，重塑了北德克萨斯州的旅行选择。
body_en: Journalist – Aaron is an aviation and travel journalist with 14 years of experience in the travel and tourism industry. His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America.

Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand.
His work has been published in Simple Flying and featured by MSN, SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel, EIN News, Pakistan Defence, and Climate Depot.

Dallas has finally gained scheduled flight operations from the city's third airport, Dallas McKinney National Airport (DTX). The airport is located to the north of the Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex and has already become Avelo Airlines' second busiest airport in its network .

For ultra-low-cost carrier Avelo , the first route for the airline from McKinney was nonstop to Fort Myers in Florida. The service departed last Wednesday and was quickly followed by Orlando and Las Vegas as the airline's first three domestic services. More flights were added on November 19, with Fort Lauderdale and Tampa taking flight.
Avelo Begins Flight Operations at Dallas-McKinney National Airport

Following the opening of the airport's new terminal and facilities, Avelo has become the first scheduled operator at the airport. The airport was the first in Texas to be granted an FAA Part 139 Airport Operating Certificate since 2005. Avelo picked McKinney to serve the fast-growing suburbs of North Texas, and provides a smaller-airport alternative when compared to the much busier Dallas/Fort Worth (DFW) and Dallas-Love Field (DAL).
McKinney's operational structure fits in well with Avelo's low-cost structure, and the airline is primarily focusing on leisure routes, such as Nevada and Florida.

With the first three routes already operating, two more beginning on November 19, and six more to be added before Christmas, McKinney's total network is 11 nonstop destinations. This has helped the airport become the airline's second-largest airport just weeks after opening (more on that in the next section). Below are the details of the airline's first three services to Fort Myers, Las Vegas, and Orlando
Dallas McKinney National Becomes Avelo's Second-Busiest Base

Data from Cirium indicates that in the first quarter of 2027, McKinney will become the airline's second-busiest airport by total flight departures. This would see McKinney overtake Wilmington (ILM) in Delaware and sit behind the region's busiest airport, Tweed New Haven Airport (HVN), in Connecticut.

McKinney's new passenger terminal has seen the launch of its first commercial flights by Avelo, marking the latest chapter for the airport after 40 years as a facility primarily used for general aviation. The airport is owned by the City of McKinney and is home to many business aircraft and fleets for global companies, like Texas Instruments and Toyota Motor Corporation.

In 2025, the city approved the construction of the new commercial passenger terminal for $72 million. This has now lured in Avelo as the first operator at the airport. Avelo remains the only airline to announce flights from the airport, with hometown Dallas airline Southwest already signaling it has no immediate interest in serving the airport as the 'numbers don't stack up'.
New And Upcoming Routes To Be Added By Avelo From Dallas-McKinney National

On November 19, McKinney gained two more nonstop domestic flights from Avelo, as Fort Lauderdale and Tampa began regular scheduled services. The airline will operate the route to Fort Lauderdale up to six times weekly, while Tampa sees a four-weekly rotation.

Additional flights are set to begin in December, with Atlanta , Denver, and Sarasota scheduled to all commence on December 16. This will be the airline's biggest one-day expansion from McKinney, with three new services all beginning on the same day.
The next day will be just as busy, as December 17 sees new services to Nashville (BNA), New Orleans (MSY), and West Palm Beach These services will all run twice weekly.
body_zh: 记者 – Aaron 是一名航空和旅行记者，在旅行和旅游业拥有 14 年的经验。他的背景涵盖机场运营、航空基础设施和旅游咨询，曾与新西兰、欧洲和北美的全球组织合作。
Aaron 将行业专业知识与五大洲超过 52 个国家/地区的第一手旅行经验相结合，涵盖航空公司、机场、航空政策和更广泛的旅行领域。他居住在新西兰坎特伯雷。
他的作品发表在《Simple Flying》上，并受到 MSN、SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel、EIN News、Pakistan Defence 和 Climate Depot 的专题报道。
达拉斯终于获得了该市第三个机场达拉斯麦金尼国家机场 (DTX) 的定期航班运营。该机场位于达拉斯/沃斯堡大都会以北，已成为阿维洛航空公司网络中第二繁忙的机场。
对于超低成本航空公司 Avelo 来说，该航空公司从麦金尼出发的第一条航线是直飞佛罗里达州迈尔斯堡。该航班于上周三起飞，紧随其后的是奥兰多和拉斯维加斯，成为该航空公司的首批三条国内航班。 11 月 19 日增加了更多航班，其中包括劳德代尔堡和坦帕航班。
Avelo 开始在达拉斯麦金尼国家机场运营航班
随着机场新航站楼和设施的启用，Avelo 成为该机场的第一家定期运营商。该机场是德克萨斯州自 2005 年以来第一个获得 FAA 第 139 部分机场运营证书的机场。Avelo 选择麦金尼为德克萨斯州北部快速发展的郊区提供服务，与繁忙得多的达拉斯/沃斯堡 (DFW) 和达拉斯-爱田 (DAL) 相比，该机场提供了一个较小的机场替代方案。
麦金尼的运营结构与阿维罗的低成本结构非常契合，该航空公司主要专注于休闲航线，例如内华达州和佛罗里达州。
前三条航线已投入运营，另外两条航线将于 11 月 19 日开始运营，圣诞节前还将增加 6 条航线，麦金尼的航线网络总数达到 11 个直达目的地。这帮助该机场在开业几周后就成为该航空公司的第二大机场（下一节将详细介绍）。以下是该航空公司飞往迈尔斯堡、拉斯维加斯和奥兰多的前三趟航班的详细信息
达拉斯麦金尼国家机场成为阿维洛第二繁忙的基地
Cirium 的数据表明，按航班起飞总数计算，麦金尼机场将在 2027 年第一季度成为该航空公司第二繁忙的机场。这将使麦金尼机场超越特拉华州的威尔明顿机场 (ILM)，落后于该地区最繁忙的机场——康涅狄格州的特威德纽黑文机场 (HVN)。
麦金尼的新客运航站楼见证了阿维洛 (Avelo) 首个商业航班的开通，标志着该机场在 40 年来主要用于通用航空设施之后的最新篇章。该机场归麦金尼市所有，是德州仪器 (TI) 和丰田汽车公司 (Toyota Motor Corporation) 等跨国公司的许多公务飞机和机队的所在地。
2025年，该市批准耗资7200万美元建设新商业客运航站楼。现在，阿维洛已成为该机场的第一家运营商。阿维洛仍然是唯一一家宣布从该机场起飞的航班的航空公司，其家乡达拉斯航空公司西南航空已经表示，它没有立即为该机场提供服务的兴趣，因为“数字不叠加”。
Avelo 将添加从达拉斯-麦金尼国家机场出发的新航线和即将开通的航线
11 月 19 日，随着劳德代尔堡和坦帕开始定期航班服务，麦金尼又获得了两趟从阿维洛出发的直飞国内航班。该航空公司将每周运营多达六趟飞往劳德代尔堡的航线，而飞往坦帕的航线则每周运营四趟。
更多航班定于 12 月开通，其中亚特兰大、丹佛和萨拉索塔均将于 12 月 16 日开通。这将是该航空公司从麦金尼起飞的最大单日航班扩张计划，三项新航班均于同一天开通。
第二天将同样繁忙，因为 12 月 17 日将开通飞往纳什维尔 (BNA)、新奥尔良 (MSY) 和西棕榈滩的新航班。这些航班均每周运行两班。

title_en: Why I’d Pick Economy Over Premium Economy On An Overnight Flight
title_zh: 为什么我在过夜航班上选择经济舱而不是豪华经济舱
summary: Flying Air France economy overnight, I found fixed armrests make premium economy harder to sleep in, while a row of empty economy seats can offer far more comfort.
summary_zh: 过夜乘坐法航经济舱，我发现固定扶手让高级经济舱更难入睡，而一排空的经济舱座位可以提供很远的睡眠。
body_en: I just got back to Rio after a quick trip to Ireland for Aer Lingus’ event to showcase their new A330 cabins , including its first-ever premium economy .

I flew Air France economy both ways, and I’m glad I resisted the offer of $420 during online check-in to upgrade the outbound overnight economy leg. Ironically, it was the long day-flight back where I actually wished I’d upgraded.
However, to answer the economy vs. premium economy question, it all comes down to maximising comfort, and I think this is easier to do in economy than premium economy.
Economy may be more comfortable for sleeping overnight
If, like me, sleeping upright or on your back is almost impossible, then what follows will likely apply to you.
The main reason I’m deterred to pick premium economy for overnight flights is because of the fixed armrests, where tray tables are sometimes stowed in this cabin.
Despite the extra recline and leg rest element (which sometimes makes it even harder to get comfortable), the fixed armrests restrict the ability to sleep any way other than straight like a pencil.
To make matters worse, they stop you from lying across more than one seat if you find yourself in an empty row.

It’s for that reason that I much prefer economy. While having a row to yourself isn’t guaranteed, there’s at least a chance of being able to move around the cabin, or stretch out into an empty seat. No matter where you sit or how empty the cabin is, you can’t do that in premium economy.
My economy seat selection strategy paid off, mostly
Another element of my pre-trip planning that I expect many of you to relate to is the fact it takes me so long umming and aahing over the best seat to pick.
Thanks to my Flying Blue Gold status (SkyTeam Elite Plus) , I could pick any seat in the economy cabin of the Boeing 777-200ER for free from 72 hours before departure.

I narrowed it down to an empty seat in the exit row, and the only row of three with an empty middle seat. I didn’t even consider one of the many empty middle rows of four seats in case they filled up before take off and I ended up in an aisle with no window to rest my head. Using the window or plane’s fuselage to rest my head on is the only saving grace for me when trying to sleep sitting upright.
As the empty exit seat would have the same restricting fixed partition as premium, I decided against that, too.

After the “boarding complete” announcement was made, the middle seat in my row remained empty, and there were three seats free in the middle of row 25, a row in front. I explained to the girl in the aisle seat that if one of us moved to the other row, we’d both have three seats to ourselves. She didn’t seem to understand my point, and said she’d prefer to sit in the aisle than us both have three free seats to ourselves.
I didn’t want to move to the middle seats either, so I got as comfortable as I could using the middle seat and the pillow I brought from home.

In the end, I did manage to get some half decent curled up shut eye (the thick pillow protected my back from the hard parts of the seat when propped against the fuselage). However, when I went to the loo, I noticed some people in the rear cabin had got lucky and were fast asleep spread across a whole four seats.

I’m not saying economy is always a better choice than premium. For example, I’d always recommend Emirates’ pretty darn impressive premium economy over economy, because it genuinely is several steps up from economy.

If it was up to me, I’d have had a lie-flat seat for the overnight segment. I didn’t, and I’m pretty certain I got better sleep quality curled up across two seats in economy that I would have almost upright on my back in premium.
Would you ever choose economy over premium economy?
body_zh: 我刚刚回到里约热内卢，此前我曾短暂前往爱尔兰参加爱尔兰航空公司的活动，展示他们的全新 A330 客舱，包括其首个豪华经济舱。
我乘坐法航经济舱往返，很高兴在网上办理登机手续时拒绝了 420 美元升级出境隔夜经济舱的提议。讽刺的是，正是在漫长的一天回程航班中，我真希望自己能升舱。
然而，要回答经济舱与豪华经济舱的问题，一切都归结为最大限度地提高舒适度，我认为这在经济舱中比豪华经济舱更容易做到。
经济舱可能更适合过夜
如果像我一样，直立或仰卧睡觉几乎不可能，那么以下内容可能适用于您。
我不敢选择过夜航班的豪华经济舱的主要原因是固定扶手，有时在这个机舱里会存放小桌板。
尽管有额外的倾斜和腿部休息元素（有时会变得更难舒服），但固定扶手限制了除了像铅笔一样笔直睡觉之外的任何其他睡眠方式。
更糟糕的是，如果您发现自己坐在空排中，它们会阻止您躺在多个座位上。
正因为如此，我更喜欢经济。虽然不能保证自己能排成一排，但至少有机会在机舱内走动，或者在空座位上伸展身体。无论您坐在哪里或机舱有多空，您都无法在豪华经济舱中做到这一点。
我的经济舱座位选择策略大部分都得到了回报
我希望你们很多人都能理解我旅行前计划的另一个要素，那就是我花了很长时间才选择最好的座位。
凭借我的蓝天飞行金卡会员身份（天合联盟精英 Plus），我可以在出发前 72 小时内免费选择波音 777-200ER 经济舱的任何座位。
我把范围缩小到出口排的一个空座位，也是唯一一排中间有空座位的三排座位。我什至没有考虑中间许多空的四个座位中的一个，以防它们在起飞前就坐满了，而我最终来到了一条没有窗户可以休息的过道。当我试图坐直睡觉时，用窗户或飞机机身来支撑我的头是唯一的可取之处。
由于空的出口座位将具有与高级座位相同的限制性固定隔断，因此我也决定不这样做。
“登机完成”的广播发出后，我这一排中间的座位还空着，前面一排25排中间还空着三个座位。我向坐在过道座位上的女孩解释说，如果我们中的一个人搬到另一排，我们就会各自拥有三个座位。她似乎不明白我的意思，并说她宁愿坐在过道上，也不愿我们俩都有三个空座位。
我也不想搬到中间的座位，所以我尽可能地使用中间的座位和从家里带来的枕头。
最后，我确实成功地蜷缩起来闭上眼睛（当我靠在机身上时，厚厚的枕头可以保护我的背部免受座椅坚硬部分的伤害）。然而，当我去洗手间时，我发现后舱里的一些人很幸运，在整整四个座位上睡着了。
我并不是说经济舱总是比高级舱更好的选择。例如，我总是推荐阿联酋航空的高级经济舱，而不是经济舱，因为它确实比经济舱高出好几个台阶。
如果由我决定的话，我会在过夜时选择一个平躺式座位。我没有，而且我很确定我蜷缩在经济舱的两个座位上可以获得更好的睡眠质量，而在高级舱中我几乎可以直立躺着。
您会选择经济舱而不是豪华经济舱吗？

title_en: Why International First Class Has Failed At US Airlines (But Shouldn’t)
title_zh: 为什么美国航空公司的国际头等舱失败了（但不应该）
summary: American has retired its 777 first class, leaving no US airline with a true international first class. Here's why it failed, and how a boutique version could work.
summary_zh: 美国航空已经退役了 777 头等舱，美国航空公司没有一家拥有真正的国际头等舱。这就是它失败的原因，以及精品版如何
body_en: We’ve just seen American formally retire its Boeing 777 first class , and with that, no airline in the United States has a “true” international first class anymore. It’s the end of an era, because going back many decades, premium products were largely pioneered by US carriers. So I think this raises the question — why can US carriers not make first class work in a way that’s economically viable, especially as they keep talking about how premium they are?

Before we get into this, let me make sure we’re all on the same page when it comes to terms. This post isn’t about the premium cabin on domestic flights, which is often referred to as first class. Instead, it’s about international flights that have a cabin above business class, when it’s marketed as first class . So this would include airlines on my list of the world’s best first class products .
There’s demand for international first class in the US

Airline executives are divided on the merits of having an international first class cabin. Some insist that there’s no need for such a cabin, as business class has improved so much. Meanwhile others absolutely see merit to such a product.

I mean, just look at how carriers like Air France , Lufthansa , Singapore Airlines , and SWISS , are all investing in first class. I think Air France’s La Premiere first class is the perfect example of the upside such a product has for an airline

Air France’s first class pricing is in a league of its own, and management at the airline claims the product is more profitable than ever before; the idea is that the airline spends a ton on customers, but also charges them a ton
Air France’s first class is all about creating a seamless experience, that’s as close to private aviation as possible
Air France’s first class offers a massive halo effect for the airline, and no doubt is one of the things that gives it such premium positioning

What’s interesting is that for the airlines that succeed with first class, the single biggest market — and single biggest point of sale — is the United States. So how is it that carriers like Air France, Lufthansa, SWISS, etc., can make money offering first class to the United States (primarily targeting Americans), but US airlines seemingly can’t?

The US has way too many people with tens or hundreds of millions of dollars, or even billions of dollars. There are plenty of people who would pay to fly private, and would pay for Air France La Premiere first class, but would never consider paying the high price for first class on a US carrier, because it’s just not worth it.
Why international first class has failed at US carriers

It’s no surprise that first class at US carriers has historically failed. In many ways, it reflects the failures of the industry from decades past. In other words, first class has long been thought of as “upgrade class,” rather than something actually worth paying for. US carriers have managed to change that narrative on domestic flights, but not so much on international flights.
What explains the failure of first class at US carriers? If you ask me, here are the main factors

First class cabins were simply too big, and on too many planes — American had eight first class seats on its 777-300ERs, and back in the day, had 16 first class seats on its 777-200ERs, and that’s just way too many planes with way too many first class seats
First class was not a product worth paying for — in recent decades, first class at US carriers just hasn’t been sufficiently differentiated in terms of soft product, both in the air and on the ground

First class couldn’t deliver consistently good service — this is related to the above point, but service at US airlines is consistently inconsistent , and it’s offensive to pay for something comparable to a Michelin three-star dining experience, and then get served by someone grumpy

First class became employee class — I’m all for airline employees having their travel benefits, but when you just give away your first class product and never have empty seats, it definitely eliminates the sense of exclusivity, and it also minimizes the investment in the soft product (given how many people you’re giving it away to)
How first class could succeed at a US airline

Call it a hot take, but I think international first class absolutely could succeed at a US carrier, if done right, with a couple of caveats. Let me start with the two main hurdles that would need to be overcome, and I’ll acknowledge, this might just be the biggest issue

US carriers would have to find a way to staff first class with flight attendants who are actually professional and personable; you can’t have a top notch first class product, and then have surly people taking care of customers, so this would need to be some sort of butler levels of service (I know, the idea is probably dead on arrival)
body_zh: 我们刚刚看到美国航空正式退役其波音 777 头等舱，从此，美国没有一家航空公司再拥有“真正的”国际头等舱。这是一个时代的结束，因为几十年前，高端产品主要是由美国运营商开创的。所以我认为这提出了一个问题——为什么美国航空公司不能以经济上可行的方式提供头等舱服务，尤其是当他们一直在谈论头等舱的溢价时？
在我们开始讨论之前，让我确保我们在条款方面达成共识。这篇文章不是关于国内航班的高级舱，通常被称为头等舱。相反，它是关于拥有商务舱以上客舱的国际航班，而其营销时是头等舱。因此，这将把航空公司列入我的世界最佳头等舱产品清单中。
美国对国际头等舱有需求
航空公司高管对于拥有国际头等舱的好处存在分歧。一些人坚持认为不需要这样的客舱，因为商务舱已经有了很大的改进。与此同时，其他人绝对看到了这种产品的优点。
我的意思是，看看法国航空、汉莎航空、新加坡航空和瑞士航空等航空公司是如何投资头等舱的。我认为法航的 La Premiere 头等舱是这种产品对航空公司的优势的完美例子
法航的头等舱定价处于领先地位，该航空公司的管理层声称该产品比以往任何时候都更有利可图；这个想法是，航空公司在客户身上花费了大量资金，但也向他们收取了大量费用
法航的头等舱致力于创造无缝体验，尽可能接近私人航空
法航的头等舱为该航空公司带来了巨大的光环效应，这无疑也是其如此高端定位的原因之一
有趣的是，对于在头等舱方面取得成功的航空公司来说，最大的市场和最大的销售点是美国。那么，为什么像法航、汉莎航空、瑞士国际航空等航空公司向美国提供头等舱（主要针对美国人）就能赚钱，而美国航空公司却似乎不能呢？
美国拥有数千万、数亿美元、甚至数十亿美元的人太多了。有很多人愿意花钱乘坐私人飞机，愿意支付法航头等舱的费用，但永远不会考虑支付高价乘坐美国航空公司的头等舱，因为这根本不值得。
为什么美国航空公司的国际头等舱失败了
美国航空公司的头等舱历来失败也就不足为奇了。在很多方面，它反映了该行业过去几十年的失败。换句话说，头等舱长期以来一直被认为是“升级舱”，而不是真正值得付费的东西。美国航空公司已经成功地改变了国内航班的这种说法，但在国际航班上却没有那么多。
如何解释美国航空公司头等舱的失败？如果你问我，主要因素如下
头等舱太大了，飞机也太多了——美国航空在 777-300ER 上有 8 个头等舱座位，而以前在 777-200ER 上有 16 个头等舱座位，飞机太多了，头等舱座位也太多了
头等舱并不是一个值得花钱购买的产品——近几十年来，美国航空公司的头等舱在空中和地面的软产品方面都没有足够的差异化
头等舱无法提供始终如一的优质服务——这与上述观点有关，但美国航空公司的服务始终不一致，而且花钱购买可与米其林三星级餐饮体验相媲美的服务，然后得到脾气暴躁的人的服务，这是一种冒犯
头等舱变成了员工舱——我完全支持航空公司员工享有旅行福利，但是当你只是赠送你的头等舱产品并且永远没有空座位时，它肯定消除了排他性感，并且还最大限度地减少了对软产品的投资（考虑到你将其赠送给多少人）
美国航空公司的头等舱如何取得成功
可以说这是一个热门话题，但我认为，如果做得好，国际头等舱绝对可以在美国航空公司取得成功，但有一些注意事项。让我从需要克服的两个主要障碍开始，我承认，这可能是最大的问题
美国航空公司必须找到一种方法来为头等舱配备真正专业且风度翩翩的空乘人员；你不可能拥有一流的一流产品，然后让脾气暴躁的人来照顾顾客，所以这需要某种管家级别的服务（我知道，这个想法可能在到达时就死了）

body_en: Three killed in Piper Comanche crash at Grand Canyon - Aviation24.be

Three people died when a Piper PA-24 Comanche registered N7217P crashed near the North Rim of Arizona’s Grand Canyon on 15 November 2026, according to US authorities. The FAA said the accident occurred at around 19:15 local time.

The Grand Canyon Regional Communications Center received a missing-aircraft report at approximately 23:30 that evening. Search teams focused on the Basin area, the aircraft’s last known location, with the Arizona Department of Public Safety using infrared equipment and night vision during an overnight aerial search.

The wreckage and debris field were located at about 10:15 on 16 November. The National Park Service confirmed there were no survivors and withheld the occupants’ names out of respect for their families.

The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating. It described the crash site as mountainous terrain and said the wreckage would be documented before being recovered for further examination. The cause has yet to be determined.

title_en: FAA orders Boeing 737NG checks over loss-of-control risk
title_zh: FAA 下令波音 737NG 检查失控风险
summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered repeated checks on certain Boeing 737 Next Generation aircraft, having… The post FAA orders Boeing 737NG checks over loss-of-control risk appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 已下令对某些下一代波音 737 飞机进行重复检查……
body_en: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered repeated checks on certain Boeing 737 Next Generation aircraft, having identified a fault that could prevent an autothrottle safety system from responding to unequal engine thrust, potentially leading to a loss of control.
The airworthiness directive (AD) covers an estimated 300 US-registered aircraft. It is scheduled for publication on November 20, 2026, and takes effect 15 days later.

The problem involves missing or incorrect spoiler-position data used by the autothrottle’s cruise thrust split monitor. Without reliable data, the monitor could fail to activate, allowing a large difference in engine thrust to develop without the autothrottle disengaging.
This could cause the aircraft to roll unexpectedly. If pilots do not recognize and correct the condition promptly, they could lose control, the FAA said.

The agency bypassed the normal advance public-comment process, citing the safety risk. Operators must perform recurring built-in tests of the digital flight control system, correct failures and repeat testing until the system passes.
The directive, AD 2026-23-04, applies to specified 737-600, -700, -700C, -800 and -900 aircraft. It does not cover the 737 MAX.
The FAA addressed a similar concern on older 737 Classic aircraft in October 2022, when it ordered repeated tests on certain 737-300, -400 and -500 models.

In that directive, the agency noted that a failed spoiler sensor could go undetected by the autothrottle computer. A review found that maintenance testing was needed to identify failures involving the sensor input or its wiring.

The necessary test had already appeared in the aircraft maintenance manual, but operators were not required to perform it repeatedly. The 2022 rule made recurring testing mandatory, to prevent a failure from remaining undetected.

body_zh: 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 在发现可能阻止自动油门安全系统响应不均匀的发动机推力并可能导致失控的故障后，已下令对某些下一代波音 737 飞机进行重复检查。
适航指令 (AD) 涵盖约 300 架在美国注册的飞机。计划于2026年11月20日发布，15天后生效。
该问题涉及自动油门巡航推力分离监视器使用的扰流板位置数据丢失或不正确。如果没有可靠的数据，监视器可能无法启动，从而导致发动机推力产生巨大差异而自动油门不脱离。
这可能会导致飞机意外滚动。美国联邦航空局表示，如果飞行员不及时识别并纠正这种情况，他们可能会失去控制。
该机构以存在安全风险为由，绕过了正常的预先公众意见征询程序。操作员必须对数字飞行控制系统进行重复的内置测试，纠正故障并重复测试，直到系统通过。
美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 于 2022 年 10 月对旧型 737 Classic 飞机提出了类似的担忧，当时它下令对某些 737-300、-400 和 -500 型号进行重复测试。
在该指令中，该机构指出，自动油门计算机可能无法检测到出现故障的扰流板传感器。审查发现需要进行维护测试来识别涉及传感器输入或其接线的故障。
必要的测试已经出现在飞机维护手册中，但操作员不需要重复执行。 2022 年规则强制要求进行定期测试，以防止故障未被发现。
