title_en: End Of An Era: American Retires Boeing 777 Flagship First Class
title_zh: 一个时代的终结：美国航空退役波音 777 旗舰头等舱
summary: American has stopped selling first class on its Boeing 777-300ERs, so no US carrier offers international first class anymore. New business class suites are coming.
summary_zh: 美国航空已停止销售其波音 777-300ER 的头等舱，因此美国航空公司不再提供国际头等舱。全新商务舱套房
body_en: American Airlines has just officially “retired” its Flagship First product on the Boeing 777-300ER, meaning that no US carrier offers an international first class product anymore. The good news is that an updated business class product is in the process of being rolled out, and that’s something that should benefit a lot of travelers.
American no longer sells its Boeing 777-300ER first class

As I’ve covered in the past, American is in the process of eliminating its “premium” first class product , and that change was just implemented for flights as of this week on the carrier’s biggest planes.

Specifically, the Boeing 777-300ER is American’s “flagship” aircraft, with 20 of the planes in the fleet. As of this week, the airline is no longer selling first class on these planes. Now, plenty of 777-300ERs with these cabins are still flying around, as American has just started reconfiguring its 777-300ERs with new cabins , including the new business class.

Still, for flights effective immediately, first class seats are just being sold as standard business class seats, and any business class passenger can select seats in the first two rows (you’d think they’d try to charge extra or at least reserve them for select elite members, but nope). So there will no longer be a differentiated soft product… not that there was much of a difference as of late anyway!

With this change, no US carrier offers an international first class product anymore either, so it very much is the end of an era. American’s 777 first class seats were controversial — on the one hand, I kind of love how they swivel, though on the other hand, they really lack privacy, and the soft product left a lot to be desired.

I expect we’ll continue to see these planes flying around well into late 2027, or possibly even into 2028, depending on how fast the retrofit project happens. American’s dedicated first class ground product has also largely been discontinued, as Flagship First Dining has turned into Flagship Dining , so a la carte lounge dining is now available to eligible business class passengers as well.

It’s great that these planes will be getting new business class suites, as they’ll also be the aircraft belonging to a US carrier with the most business class seats, as they’ll have 70 of them… that’s lot!
American’s A321T first class is around until March 2027

While American has now eliminated its international first class product, it’s worth emphasizing that the airline still technically has a “premium” first class, in the sense of a cabin above business class.

Specifically, American still has its specially configured Airbus A321T aircraft, which are used primarily for flights between New York (JFK) and Los Angeles (LAX) and San Francisco (SFO). The planes have 10 reverse herringbone seats spread across five rows, in a 1-1 configuration.
American also plans to eliminate this product, as the A321Ts will be reconfigured into standard A321 domestic configuration aircraft, and A321XLRs will be taking over the transcon routes.

American has stopped selling first class on these planes for flights as of March 28, 2027. After that date we’ll still see some of the planes flying with the cabins, but the first class seats will simply be sold as business class.

American Airlines has officially eliminated its international first class product, as Boeing 777-300ERs no longer have Flagship First for sale. These planes are being retrofitted, as first class seats are being eliminated, and new business class suites are being introduced. However, the planes will keep flying around with the current cabins for quite some time, and business class passengers can freely assign the first class seats.
In the spring, we’ll see American eliminate its last “premium” first class product, which is the A321T first class cabin, as those planes are replaced by A321XLRs.
What do you make of the end of American’s Flagship First on the 777?
body_zh: 美国航空刚刚正式“退役”了波音 777-300ER 上的旗舰头等舱产品，这意味着美国航空公司不再提供国际头等舱产品。好消息是，更新的商务舱产品正在推出，这应该会让很多旅客受益。
美国航空不再销售其波音 777-300ER 头等舱
正如我过去所介绍的，美国航空正在取消其“优质”头等舱产品，并且这一变化刚刚在本周该航空公司最大的飞机上实施。
具体来说，波音 777-300ER 是美国航空的“旗舰”飞机，机队中有 20 架飞机。截至本周，该航空公司不再销售这些飞机的头等舱。现在，大量配备这些客舱的 777-300ER 仍在飞行，因为美国航空刚刚开始为其 777-300ER 重新配置新客舱，包括新的商务舱。
不过，对于立即生效的航班，头等舱座位只是作为标准商务舱座位出售，任何商务舱乘客都可以选择前两排的座位（你可能会认为他们会尝试收取额外费用或至少为精选的精英会员保留座位，但事实并非如此）。因此，将不再有差异化的软产品……无论如何，最近并没有太大的差异！
随着这一变化，美国航空公司也不再提供国际一流的产品，因此这在很大程度上是一个时代的结束。美国航空的 777 头等舱座椅颇受争议——一方面，我有点喜欢它们的旋转方式，但另一方面，它们确实缺乏隐私，而且软质产品还有很多不足之处。
我预计这些飞机将继续飞行到 2027 年末，甚至可能持续到 2028 年，具体取决于改造项目的进展速度。美国航空专用的头等舱地面产品也已基本停止，因为旗舰头等舱餐饮已转变为旗舰餐饮，因此符合条件的商务舱乘客现在也可以使用点菜休息室餐饮。
很高兴这些飞机将配备新的商务舱套房，因为它们也将成为拥有最多商务舱座位的美国航空公司的飞机，因为他们将拥有 70 个商务舱座位……这太多了！
美国航空 A321T 头等舱将于 2027 年 3 月到期
虽然美国航空现在已经取消了其国际头等舱产品，但值得强调的是，从技术上讲，该航空公司仍然拥有“高级”头等舱，即高于商务舱的舱位。
具体来说，美国航空仍然拥有专门配置的空客A321T飞机，主要用于纽约（JFK）与洛杉矶（LAX）和旧金山（SFO）之间的航班。这些飞机有 10 个反向人字形座椅，分布在五排，呈 1-1 布局。
美国航空还计划淘汰该产品，因为A321T将被重新配置为标准A321国内配置飞机，而A321XLR将接管​​转运航线。
自 2027 年 3 月 28 日起，美国航空已停止在这些飞机上销售头等舱。在此日期之后，我们仍会看到一些带有客舱的飞机飞行，但头等舱座位将仅作为商务舱出售。
美国航空已正式淘汰其国际头等舱产品，波音 777-300ER 不再出售旗舰头等舱。这些飞机正在进行改装，头等舱座位正在被淘汰，而新的商务舱套房正在推出。不过，飞机将在相当一段时间内继续沿现有舱位飞行，公务舱乘客可以自由分配头等舱座位。
今年春天，我们将看到美国航空淘汰其最后一款“优质”头等舱产品，即 A321T 头等舱，因为这些飞机将被 A321XLR 所取代。

Support includes innovative technology assessment and development; rapid software development and prototyping; enabling capability training; security engineering; and cybersecurity risk management. This is one of four multiple-award contracts. All awardees will have the opportunity to compete for task orders during the ordering period. The Space and Naval Warfare Systems Center Pacific, San Diego, is the contracting activity (N66001-17-D-0117). Selected U.S. military contracts for March 9, 2017 U.S. MISSILE DEFENSE AGENCY Lockheed Martin Space Systems Co. , Sunnyvale, California, was awarded a $53,052,807 competitive cost-plus-fixed-fee contract for a 36-month period with no options for the Multi-Object Kill Vehicle Technology Risk Reduction (TRR) effort. This contract represents part of the Missile Defense Agency’s technology risk reduction strategy to improve performance and reduce risk for a gimbaled seeker assembly, integrated avionics assembly, component integration and testing, and an advanced seeker. The Missile Defense Agency, Huntsville, Alabama, is the contracting activity (HQ0147-17-C-0002). U.S. NAVY ViON Corp. , Herndon, California, is being awarded a $34,790,000 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract to provide Capacity as a Service support to Space and Naval Warfare Systems Command (Spawar) Headquarters, Spawar System Center Pacific and Spawar System Center Atlantic. The Capacity as a Service acquisition model allows Spawar to more accurately scale, up and down, its information technology (IT) infrastructure to meet evolving mission requirements. Savings are realized through no up-front costs and a “pay as you go” acquisition model, reducing waste usually associated with overbuying of IT equipment to eventually meet an expectation of mission requirement. Under this contract, ViON is responsible for providing on-demand, on-premise computing, networking and storage solutions for a variety of systems and applications for the command’s research, development, testing and evaluation core infrastructures, laboratory and data center environments. This contract includes options, which if exercised, would bring the maximum contract value to $49,990,000. The Space and Naval Warfare Systems Command, San Diego, is the contracting activity (N00039-17-D-0003).
